## Four Pillars Section

### Section Headline
Care that meets you where you are

### Section Intro
Whether you have been putting off a fistula surgery for years, need a hernia repair before a family event, or want to understand whether your piles actually need surgery at all, we listen first, examine carefully, and recommend the treatment that fits your case, your body, and your life. Not every condition needs surgery. When it does, you have options. We help you choose.

### Pillar 1: Advanced Anorectal Care
**Icon:** Anorectal specialty icon

**Title:** Advanced Anorectal Care

**Description:** Piles, fissure, fistula, pilonidal sinus, and complex or recurrent cases. Treatment options across the full spectrum: office-based interventions, Ksharsutra, laser proctology, and conventional surgery.

**Link:** Explore Anorectal Care →

### Pillar 2: General Surgery
**Icon:** Surgery icon

**Title:** General Surgery

**Description:** Hernia, hydrocele, appendicitis, gall bladder disease, breast lump, lipoma, and other general surgical needs. Modern techniques with careful pre and post-operative care.

**Link:** Explore General Surgery →

### Pillar 3: Ayurveda and Panchakarma
**Icon:** Ayurveda icon

**Title:** Ayurveda and Panchakarma

**Description:** Classical Ayurvedic treatment and Panchakarma therapies for hyperacidity, spine conditions, sciatica, skin diseases, non-healing wounds, and more. Delivered by qualified Ayurvedic surgeons.

**Link:** Explore Ayurveda and Panchakarma →

**Icon:** Specialty icon

**Link:** Explore Specialty Care →

## Doctors Section

### Section Headline
Meet Your Specialists

### Section Intro
Shri Manmukund Hospital is led by two MS Ayurveda Shalya Tantra specialists working together as a clinical team. Between us, we cover the full range of anorectal, general surgical, and integrated Ayurvedic practice, with a division of focus that ensures every patient sees the right specialist for their case.

**Photograph:** Environmental portrait, brand palette background.

**Name:** Dr. Vipin Tongale

**Specialisations:** Anorectal Surgery, Complex and Recurrent Cases, Ksharsutra, Laser Proctology, Uttarbasti (Stricture Urethra), General Surgery

### Doctor Card: Dr. Swati Tongale

**Photograph:** Environmental portrait, brand palette background.

**Name:** Dr. Swati Tongale

**Credentials:** MS Ayurveda Shalya Tantra

**Role:** General Surgeon and Proctologist, Female Specialty Care Lead

**Specialisations:** Female Proctology, Uttarbasti for Infertility, Ayurvedic Care for Women, Panchakarma

**Summary:** MS Ayurveda Shalya Tantra specialist with dedicated focus on female proctology and Uttarbasti-based fertility care. For female patients who prefer a female specialist for sensitive anorectal and gynaecological procedures.

**CTA:** View Dr. Swati's Page →

---

## Why Us Section

### Section Headline
Why patients choose Shri Manmukund Hospital

### Six Trust Factors

**Full-spectrum options.** Ksharsutra, laser proctology, non-surgical interventions, and conventional surgery are all offered. Instead of pushing a single technique, we help you choose the one that fits your condition, your grade of disease, and your recovery timeline.

**Two MS specialists.** Both consultants are MS Ayurveda Shalya Tantra qualified surgeons, not general practitioners referring you elsewhere for surgical work. Your consultation, examination, procedure, and follow-up are all under specialist care.

**Female specialist available.** Dr. Swati handles female patients directly for anorectal, gynaecological Ayurvedic, and Uttarbasti-based fertility care. Many female patients delay seeking help for anorectal problems because of male-doctor discomfort. We remove that barrier inside our own hospital.

**Complex cases welcome.** Recurrent fistula, non-healing wounds, cases that other clinics have already tried and failed, these are our routine work. If you have been told your condition is "difficult" elsewhere, ask us for a second opinion.

**On-site facility.** Own operation theatre, Panchakarma section, four-bed ward, and attached Anvi Medical pharmacy. Your consultation, procedure, and medicines happen under one roof. No shuttling between facilities.

**Honest counselling.** We recommend the treatment that is right for the patient, not the one most convenient for the practice. If your case does not need surgery, we will tell you.

**URL:** `/about/`
**Meta title:** About Shri Manmukund Hospital, Amravati | Our Story Since 2011
**Meta description:** A hospital that began as an OPD in 2011, became a hospital in 2016, and moved to its own facility in 2024. Two MS Ayurveda specialists. Integrated surgical and Ayurvedic care.

---

## Hero

### Headline
Our Story

### Sub-headline
From a small OPD in 2011 to a full-facility hospital today, built one patient at a time.

---

## Timeline Section

### Section Headline
Three moments that shaped us

### Milestone 1
**Date:** 6 June 2011
**Title:** The OPD begins
**Description:** Dr. Vipin Tongale opens a specialist OPD in Amravati, offering proctology, general surgery consultation, and Ayurvedic care. Dr. Swati joins the practice as clinical partner shortly after. The philosophy is set from day one: patients deserve the right treatment, not the most convenient one.

### Milestone 2
**Date:** 28 October 2016
**Title:** OPD becomes a hospital
**Description:** After five years of growing patient trust, the OPD upgrades to a full hospital at a rented facility. Operation theatre, Panchakarma section, ward, and pharmacy all come together under one roof. The hospital can now handle surgical admissions, post-operative care, and Panchakarma programmes on site.

### Milestone 3
**Date:** 1 June 2024
**Title:** Our own hospital
**Description:** The hospital moves to its own permanent facility at Bapatwadi, Amravati. Dedicated consultation chambers for both doctors, a four-bed ward, a well-equipped operation theatre, a Panchakarma unit with associated therapy rooms, and the attached Anvi Medical pharmacy come together in a purpose-built setup.

---

## Philosophy Section

### Section Headline
What we believe

### Body Copy
We believe that surgery is a serious decision, and every patient deserves an honest conversation before it. We believe that classical Ayurvedic surgical practice, when it fits the case, is medicine. Not alternative medicine, not folk medicine: medicine. We believe that modern minimally invasive techniques, when they fit the case, should be offered without hesitation.

We believe that a female patient should have the choice of a female specialist for sensitive care. We believe that when a patient has already been through failed treatment elsewhere, they deserve extra care, not extra caution.

And we believe that a hospital is built one patient at a time, through outcomes and honesty, not through advertising.

---

## Facilities Section

### Section Headline
Our facilities

### Section Intro
Everything a specialist proctology and integrated surgical practice needs, on one site.

### Facility Cards

**Operation Theatre**
Fully equipped OT for anorectal procedures, hernia repair, hydrocele surgery, laser proctology, Ksharsutra procedures, and general surgical cases.

**Panchakarma Unit**
Dedicated Panchakarma therapy space with equipment for classical five-therapy programmes, Uttarbasti, Swedan (steam therapy), and specialised local therapies such as Kati Basti and Greeva Basti.

**Ward and Special Room**
Four-bed ward with clean, comfortable arrangements. Attached AC special room for patients who prefer additional privacy during recovery.

**Two Consultation Chambers**
Separate consultation chambers for Dr. Vipin and Dr. Swati, allowing simultaneous consultations and preserving patient privacy.

**Anvi Medical Pharmacy**
Attached in-house pharmacy stocking both allopathic and Ayurvedic medicines. Prescriptions filled without leaving the premises.

**24-Hour Availability**
The hospital is open 24 hours. Emergency cases are attended throughout the day and night. Planned surgeries typically happen in the morning.

---

## Team Section

### Section Headline
The team behind Shri Manmukund

### Sub-section: Doctors

**Dr. Vipin Tongale**
MS Ayurveda Shalya Tantra, PhD Shalya Tantra
General Surgeon and Proctologist
[Link to /dr-vipin/]

**Dr. Swati Tongale**
MS Ayurveda Shalya Tantra
General Surgeon and Proctologist, Female Specialty Care Lead
[Link to /dr-swati/]

### Sub-section: Support Staff

Our team includes trained Panchakarma therapists, nursing staff, and OT technicians. Every member of the team is oriented toward patient dignity, especially in anorectal and sensitive care settings.

---

## Affiliations and Recognition

### Section Headline
Affiliations and academic engagement

### Body Copy
Dr. Vipin Tongale has served under the AYUSH ministry at District Hospital Amravati for 12 years and continues as an honorary surgeon at Shri Gurudev Ayurved Mahavidyalaya, Gurukunj Ashram, Mozari. Both doctors participate in continuing medical education, publication, and knowledge sharing within the Ayurvedic surgical community.

Detailed publications, awards, and recognition are listed on the individual doctor pages.

---

## Visit Us

### Section Headline
Come and see for yourself

### Body Copy
The best way to understand what we do is to come in for a consultation. We take walk-ins during OPD hours, but a prior appointment reduces your wait. If you are travelling from outside Amravati, please call ahead so we can guide you on timing and travel.

### CTAs
Book a Consultation | Call 8208927917 | View Location

## About Section

### Section Headline
About Dr. Vipin

### Answer-first Summary
Dr. Vipin Tongale is an MS and PhD Ayurveda Shalya Tantra specialist practising as a General Surgeon and Proctologist in Amravati, Maharashtra. He has performed over 16,000 surgical procedures across three institutions since 2011, including 12 years of AYUSH government service at District Hospital Amravati.

### Body Copy
Dr. Vipin's practice sits at the intersection of classical Ayurvedic surgical tradition and modern minimally invasive proctology. This is deliberate. Neither approach is complete on its own, and neither is right for every patient. What is right, in his view, is a doctor who can honestly evaluate a case, present the actual options, and let the patient choose with full information.

His clinical focus is proctology, particularly complex and recurrent cases where earlier treatment has failed. Alongside this, he handles a full general surgical workload: hernia, hydrocele, appendicitis, breast lump, lipoma, sebaceous cyst, and other cases. On the Ayurvedic side, his Uttarbasti practice for stricture urethra is well-established, and he offers Panchakarma-integrated care for spine conditions, hyperacidity, and non-healing wounds.

He is also a teacher and continuing scholar. His PhD in Shalya Tantra, honorary surgeon role at Shri Gurudev Ayurved Mahavidyalaya, and ongoing publications reflect a commitment to the academic side of Ayurvedic surgery, not just the private practice.

---

## Areas of Expertise

### Section Headline
Areas of Expertise

### Expertise Cards

**Anorectal Surgery**
Piles, anal fissure, anal fistula (including recurrent and complex), pilonidal sinus, perianal abscess, rectal prolapse. Treatment across the full spectrum: conservative, non-surgical (rubber band ligation, sclerotherapy), Ksharsutra, laser, and conventional surgery.

**Ksharsutra**
Classical Ayurvedic parasurgical technique for anal fistula and select other anorectal conditions. A signature area of practice with over a decade of dedicated case volume.

**Laser Proctology**
Modern minimally invasive procedures including laser haemorrhoidoplasty (LHP), laser fistula treatment (FiLaC), and laser treatment for pilonidal sinus. Day-care procedures with faster return to work.

**Uttarbasti for Stricture Urethra**
Panchakarma-based Ayurvedic management of urethral stricture. A specialised area developed over years of clinical practice with careful case selection.

**General Surgery**
Hernia repair, hydrocele surgery, appendicectomy, breast lump excision, lipoma removal, sebaceous cyst removal, abscess drainage, wound debridement.

**Wound Management**
Special interest in non-healing wounds and diabetic ulcers. Integrated Ayurvedic and modern wound care protocols. Also offers Jalaukavacharana (leech therapy) for indicated cases.

**Panchakarma for Vata Disorders**
Classical Panchakarma programmes for spine conditions (cervical spondylosis, lumbar spondylosis, sciatica), Vata vikara, and chronic hyperacidity.

---

## Professional Journey

### Section Headline
Professional Journey

### Body Copy
Female patients with anorectal problems, whether piles, fissure, fistula, or related conditions, often delay seeking help for months or years because the thought of examination by a male doctor is uncomfortable. Dr. Swati exists in the practice precisely to remove that barrier. Female patients at Shri Manmukund Hospital have the choice of a female specialist for consultation, examination, procedure, and follow-up, all inside the same hospital.

---

## Hero

### Headline
Advanced Anorectal Care Unit

### Sub-headline
Specialist treatment for piles, fissure, fistula, pilonidal sinus, and complex or recurrent anorectal conditions. Options across the full treatment spectrum, chosen for your case.

### Primary CTA
Book a Consultation

### Secondary CTA
Call 8208927917

---

## Introduction

The anorectal region deserves specialist attention. Conditions here are common, distressing, and highly treatable when addressed properly. They are also, unfortunately, one of the most delayed presentations in medicine. Patients wait months or years before consulting a doctor, either from embarrassment or from hope that the problem will resolve on its own. It rarely does.

At Shri Manmukund Hospital, our Advanced Anorectal Care Unit is our flagship service. It is led by two MS Ayurveda Shalya Tantra specialists who have collectively performed thousands of anorectal procedures using a full range of techniques. Our commitment is to treat every anorectal patient with the dignity, honesty, and thoroughness the specialty demands.

---

## Conditions We Treat

Eight-card grid, each linking to the condition page:

- Piles (Haemorrhoids)
- Anal Fissure
- Anal Fistula (Fistula-in-Ano)
- Recurrent Anal Fistula
- Perianal Abscess
- Pilonidal Sinus
- Rectal Prolapse
- Female Proctology

---

## Four Tiers of Treatment

### Section Intro
Rather than pushing a single technique, we offer the full range of options and choose based on your specific condition, its grade, and your circumstances.

### Tier 1: Conservative and Lifestyle
Suitable for early-stage conditions. Includes dietary modification, high-fibre intake, topical and oral medication, and other non-invasive measures. Many patients can be managed at this tier if the condition is caught early.

### Tier 2: Non-Surgical OPD Interventions
Office-based procedures for piles including rubber band ligation and injection sclerotherapy. Alongside these, Matra Basti (small-volume medicated oil enema) is used for anal fissure and chronic constipation as an OPD-based Panchakarma intervention. Performed in the consultation setting, usually without anaesthesia, with same-day discharge and next-day return to work.
[Link to Non-Surgical Piles Interventions hub]

### Tier 3a: Ksharsutra and Related Ayurvedic Surgical Techniques
Classical Ayurvedic parasurgical approach for anal fistula (all types including complex and recurrent) and select other anorectal conditions. Techniques include Ksharsutra thread application, Partial Fistulectomy with Ksharsutra Ligation, and IFTAK (Interception of Fistula Tract And Ksharsutra) for select complex or recurrent cases. Ksharkarma is used for internal piles. Over 15 years of dedicated practice at our hospital.

Note: Ksharsutra is not used for anal fissure. For chronic fissure, Matra Basti with Ayurvedic medication is our preferred non-surgical Ayurvedic approach.
[Link to Ksharsutra hub]

### Tier 3b: Laser Proctology (Modern Minimally Invasive)
Modern diode laser techniques including Laser Haemorrhoidoplasty (LHP), Laser Fistula Treatment (FiLaC), and laser pilonidal sinus treatment (SiLaC). Sphincter-preserving and typically day-care.
[Link to Laser Proctology hub]

### Tier 4: Conventional Surgery
Traditional surgical procedures where advanced or complex disease requires them. Performed with modern anaesthesia and careful post-operative care.

---

## What Makes Our Unit Different

### Full-spectrum options
All four treatment tiers offered under one roof. Very few practices in Vidarbha offer this combined range honestly.

### Complex and recurrent cases welcome
Our practice regularly sees patients whose earlier treatment elsewhere has failed. Complex fistula, recurrent piles after surgery, non-healing perianal wounds are part of our routine work.

### Female specialist available
Dr. Swati provides direct consultation, examination, and procedural care for female patients who prefer a female specialist for sensitive anorectal work.

### One hospital for the entire journey
Consultation, diagnostic evaluation, procedure, recovery, and follow-up all happen in the same facility. No shuttling between locations.

### Honest counselling
If your case can be managed conservatively, we say so. If it needs surgery, we explain why. If multiple options exist, we present all of them with their trade-offs.

### Continuing scholarship
Our contributions to Ksharsutra literature and Ayurvedic surgical practice reflect commitment to the specialty beyond private practice.

---

## Meet Your Specialists

Doctor cards for Dr. Vipin Tongale and Dr. Swati Tongale, side by side, equal treatment.

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Do all anorectal conditions need surgery?**
No. Many anorectal conditions can be managed with lifestyle changes, medication, or office-based procedures. Surgery is recommended only when it is genuinely the best option for the patient.

**Q: Is anorectal examination painful?**
The examination is uncomfortable but rarely painful. Modern practice includes lubrication, small-diameter instruments, and unhurried technique to minimise discomfort. Female patients may specifically request Dr. Swati.

**Q: How long is recovery after anorectal treatment?**
Recovery varies dramatically by procedure. Office-based procedures often allow same-day return to work. Laser procedures typically need 2 to 5 days. Ksharsutra involves weekly follow-up over 4 to 8 weeks. Conventional surgery may require 1 to 2 weeks of recovery.

**Q: Do you offer day-care procedures?**
Yes. Rubber band ligation, sclerotherapy, laser haemorrhoidoplasty, laser fistula treatment, and many minor procedures are day-care. Patients arrive in the morning and go home the same day.

**Q: Do you accept insurance?**
Shri Manmukund Hospital is registered under ROHINI (Registry of Hospitals in Network of Insurance), which is the national identifier system for hospitals under insurance networks. For cashless treatment, we currently carry select cases through partner hospital arrangements while our own cashless empanelment is under process. Please call 8208927917 for current information on insurance panels and cashless options for your specific insurer.

**Q: Can I speak to the doctor before coming in?**
Yes. We understand anorectal problems are sensitive. Call 8208927917 to arrange a preliminary phone or WhatsApp discussion before your first visit.

**Q: What if I have already been treated elsewhere and the problem returned?**
Recurrent and complex cases are a core part of our practice. Please bring any previous reports, discharge summaries, or operative notes when you visit.

---

- Article: When Does an Anal Fistula Need Surgery?

All four treatment tiers offered under one roof. Very few practices in Vidarbha offer this combined range honestly.

### Complex and recurrent cases welcome
Our practice regularly sees patients whose earlier treatment elsewhere has failed. Complex fistula, recurrent piles after surgery, non-healing perianal wounds are part of our routine work.

Dr. Swati provides direct consultation, examination, and procedural care for female patients who prefer a female specialist for sensitive anorectal work.

Consultation, diagnostic evaluation, procedure, recovery, and follow-up all happen in the same facility. No shuttling between locations.

If your case can be managed conservatively, we say so. If it needs surgery, we explain why. If multiple options exist, we present all of them with their trade-offs.

Our contributions to Ksharsutra literature and Ayurvedic surgical practice reflect commitment to the specialty beyond private practice.

Doctor cards for Dr. Vipin Tongale and Dr. Swati Tongale, side by side, equal treatment.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Do all anorectal conditions need surgery?**
No. Many anorectal conditions can be managed with lifestyle changes, medication, or office-based procedures. Surgery is recommended only when it is genuinely the best option for the patient.

**Q: Is anorectal examination painful?**
The examination is uncomfortable but rarely painful. Modern practice includes lubrication, small-diameter instruments, and unhurried technique to minimise discomfort. Female patients may specifically request Dr. Swati.

Recovery varies dramatically by procedure. Office-based procedures often allow same-day return to work. Laser procedures typically need 2 to 5 days. Ksharsutra involves weekly follow-up over 4 to 8 weeks. Conventional surgery may require 1 to 2 weeks of recovery.

Shri Manmukund Hospital is registered under ROHINI (Registry of Hospitals in Network of Insurance), which is the national identifier system for hospitals under insurance networks. Please call 8208927917 for current information on insurance panels and cashless options for your specific insurer.

Yes. We understand anorectal problems are sensitive. Call 8208927917 to arrange a preliminary phone or WhatsApp discussion before your first visit.

**Q: What if I have already been treated elsewhere and the problem returned?**
Recurrent and complex cases are a core part of our practice. Please bring any previous reports, discharge summaries, or operative notes when you visit.

## Hero

### Headline
Piles (Haemorrhoids) Treatment

### Alternative Names
Bawaseer (बवासीर) | Mool Vyadhi (मूळव्याध) | Arsha (Sanskrit)

### Sub-headline
Effective treatment for all grades of internal, external, and mixed piles. Options range from non-surgical OPD procedures to Ksharsutra, laser haemorrhoidoplasty, and conventional surgery.

---

## Answer-First Summary

Piles (haemorrhoids) are swollen veins in the lower rectum or anus that cause bleeding, pain, itching, or protrusion. Treatment depends on the grade: lifestyle changes and medication for early grades, office-based procedures like rubber band ligation or sclerotherapy for moderate cases, and Ksharsutra, laser haemorrhoidoplasty, or surgery for advanced cases. Not every case of piles requires surgery.

---

## What Are Piles?

Piles, also called haemorrhoids, occur when the blood vessels around the anus become swollen and inflamed. They can be internal (inside the rectum, not usually visible from outside), external (under the skin around the anus), or a combination of both.

Piles are extremely common. Estimates suggest that up to half of adults will experience piles at some point, particularly after the age of 30. Despite this, piles remain one of the most under-reported and delayed presentations in Indian outpatient practice, largely due to embarrassment.

---

## Symptoms

- Bright red bleeding during or after passing stool (the most common symptom)
- Discomfort, itching, or burning around the anus
- A soft lump felt at the anal opening (external piles)
- Feeling of incomplete evacuation after passing stool
- Mucus discharge staining underwear
- Prolapse of tissue during or after a bowel movement (advanced grades)
- Sudden severe pain and a hard tender lump (thrombosed external pile)

---

## Causes and Risk Factors

- Chronic constipation with straining
- Diet low in fibre and fluids
- Prolonged sitting, especially on the toilet with phone or reading material
- Pregnancy and childbirth
- Obesity
- Ageing (weakening of anal cushion support tissue)
- Family history of piles
- Heavy lifting or straining occupations
- Chronic cough or portal hypertension (less common)

---

## Grades of Piles

Understanding the grade of your piles matters because treatment options differ by grade.

**Grade I:** Bleeding but no prolapse. The piles remain inside.
**Grade II:** Prolapse during defecation but retract spontaneously.
**Grade III:** Prolapse that must be pushed back manually.
**Grade IV:** Permanently prolapsed. Cannot be reduced.

A specialist examination determines your grade.

---

## When to See a Specialist

Please seek a consultation for any of the following:

- Rectal bleeding, even if painless and self-limited (bleeding should never be self-diagnosed as piles; other conditions including polyps and cancer can cause similar bleeding)
- Persistent pain, itching, or lump lasting more than two weeks
- Prolapse of tissue
- Symptoms that do not improve with two weeks of dietary and lifestyle measures
- Acute severe pain with a hard lump (possible thrombosed pile needing urgent attention)

**Emergency:** Seek immediate medical care if you have heavy or continuous bleeding, dizziness, black stools, or severe unrelenting pain.

---

## Diagnosis

Piles are usually diagnosed based on history and physical examination. Depending on your age, symptoms, and history, we may recommend additional evaluation such as proctoscopy, sigmoidoscopy, or colonoscopy, particularly to rule out other causes of rectal bleeding in patients over 45 or with a family history of colorectal cancer.

Examination is conducted with attention to your comfort and privacy. Female patients may specifically request Dr. Swati.

---

## Treatment Options at Shri Manmukund Hospital

All four treatment tiers are offered. Your grade, your case, and your preferences guide the recommendation.

### Tier 1: Conservative and Lifestyle
**Suitable for:** Grade I, early Grade II
**Approach:** High-fibre diet (25 to 30 g per day), adequate fluid intake (2 to 3 litres per day), avoiding prolonged straining and toilet time, topical medications for symptom relief, oral medication where indicated.

Many early-stage patients respond well to lifestyle changes alone and do not require any procedure.

### Tier 2: Non-Surgical OPD Procedures
**Suitable for:** Grade I, Grade II, selected Grade III
**Options offered:** Rubber Band Ligation, Injection Sclerotherapy
**Duration:** 10 to 20 minutes per session
**Anaesthesia:** Usually not required
**Recovery:** Same-day discharge, return to work the next day

### Tier 3a: Ksharsutra
**Suitable for:** Advanced piles, especially with associated fistula or fissure
Classical Ayurvedic parasurgical approach with over a decade of dedicated practice at our hospital. Involves application of a medicated thread that gradually resolves the pathological tissue over weekly sessions.

### Tier 3b: Laser Haemorrhoidoplasty (LHP)
**Suitable for:** Grade II, III, and selected Grade IV
Modern minimally invasive approach using a diode laser to shrink pile tissue with minimal cutting.
**Advantages:** Less post-operative pain, minimal bleeding, faster recovery, day-care procedure, sphincter preservation.
**Recovery:** Typically 2 to 5 days before return to work.

### Tier 4: Conventional Surgery (Haemorrhoidectomy)
**Suitable for:** Advanced Grade III, Grade IV, thrombosed piles requiring urgent excision, complex cases where other tiers are unsuitable
**Approach:** Traditional surgical removal under regional or general anaesthesia.
**Recovery:** Typically 1 to 2 weeks off work with structured post-operative care.

---

## Recovery and Follow-up

Recovery depends on the tier of treatment received. Every patient receives written post-procedure instructions covering diet, activity, wound care (where applicable), and medication schedule. WhatsApp and phone support are available during recovery for questions.

**Standard follow-up schedule:** day 3, day 7, day 14, day 28, and day 42 after procedure. This structured schedule allows us to catch and address any issues early, monitor healing progression, and adjust care as needed.

**Flexible schedule for patients travelling from a distance:** For patients whose work or distance from Amravati makes frequent visits impractical, we can consolidate follow-up to day 7, day 21, and day 42, with WhatsApp and phone support between visits. Discuss your travel situation at consultation so we can plan appropriately.

---

## Prevention

- Ensure adequate fibre in your diet (25 to 30 g per day). Include fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and pulses.
- Drink adequate fluids (2 to 3 litres per day).
- Maintain regular physical activity. Even 30 minutes of walking daily helps.
- Avoid prolonged sitting on the toilet. Keep phones and reading material away.
- Do not delay the urge to defecate.
- Do not strain. If passing stool is difficult, focus on dietary correction rather than pushing harder.
- Manage weight if overweight.

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Can piles go away on their own?**
Grade I piles caused by temporary constipation may resolve with lifestyle changes. Higher grades typically do not resolve without intervention and often worsen over time if untreated.

**Q: Is bleeding during stool always due to piles?**
No. While piles are the most common cause of painless rectal bleeding, other conditions including anal fissure, polyps, inflammatory bowel disease, and colorectal cancer can cause similar bleeding. Any new rectal bleeding warrants a specialist consultation, especially over the age of 45.

**Q: What is the best treatment for piles?**
There is no single best treatment. The right treatment depends on your grade of piles, your symptoms, your general health, and your preferences. A specialist consultation is needed to determine which option fits you.

**Q: Is laser piles surgery painful?**
Laser haemorrhoidoplasty is generally less painful than conventional surgery. It is not entirely painless, but modern pain management makes recovery comfortable for most patients.

**Q: What does piles treatment cost?**
Cost varies significantly based on the treatment tier, whether the procedure is day-care or requires admission, and any additional evaluation required. Please call 8208927917 for current guidance.

**Q: Will piles come back after treatment?**
Any anorectal condition can recur, especially if the underlying risk factors (constipation, straining, low-fibre diet) are not corrected. Following prevention guidance significantly reduces recurrence.

**Q: Is there Ayurvedic treatment for piles?**
Yes. Ksharsutra is a classical Ayurvedic parasurgical approach with well-established indications, particularly for piles associated with other conditions. Panchakarma and oral Ayurvedic medication may also be used for supportive management in select cases.

**Q: Can I go to work after laser piles surgery?**
Most patients return to office work within 2 to 5 days after laser haemorrhoidoplasty. Physically demanding jobs may require slightly longer.

**Q: Should I worry about piles during pregnancy?**
Piles are common during pregnancy due to hormonal changes and pressure from the growing uterus. Most pregnancy-related piles resolve after delivery. Conservative management is preferred during pregnancy. Consult before starting any treatment.

**Q: What foods should I avoid if I have piles?**
Highly spicy foods can worsen symptoms during an acute episode. Otherwise, the focus is on adding fibre and fluids rather than restrictive elimination. Constipating foods (excessive dairy, refined flour, very low-fibre diets) should be limited.

---

**URL:** `/services/anorectal-care/anal-fissure/`
**Meta title:** Anal Fissure Treatment Amravati | Chronic Fissure Specialist
**Meta description:** Effective treatment for acute and chronic anal fissure in Amravati. Conservative, laser sphincterotomy, and Ayurvedic options by MS Ayurveda surgeons.

---

## Hero

### Headline
Anal Fissure Treatment

### Alternative Names
Fissure-in-Ano | Parikartika (Sanskrit)

### Sub-headline
Effective treatment for acute and chronic anal fissures. Most cases heal without surgery. When surgery is needed, sphincter-preserving laser and Ayurvedic options are available.

---

## Answer-First Summary

An anal fissure is a small tear in the lining of the anus, causing sharp pain during and after passing stool, often with bright red bleeding. Acute fissures usually heal within a few weeks with conservative treatment (stool softeners, sitz baths, topical medication). Chronic fissures (lasting over 6 to 8 weeks) may need laser sphincterotomy, Ksharkarma, or occasionally conventional surgery. Most patients avoid surgery entirely with early treatment.

---

## What Is an Anal Fissure?

An anal fissure is a tear or crack in the thin, moist lining (mucosa) of the anus. It typically develops after passing hard, large, or difficult stool, and once formed, is aggravated by every subsequent bowel movement.

Fissures are classified by duration:
- **Acute fissure:** less than 6 to 8 weeks. Usually heals with conservative care.
- **Chronic fissure:** over 6 to 8 weeks. Usually has secondary features (sentinel skin tag, hypertrophied papilla) and often needs procedural treatment.

---

## Symptoms

- Sharp, cutting pain during bowel movement (often described as passing broken glass)
- Pain continuing for several hours after passing stool
- Bright red bleeding, usually a small amount on toilet paper or the stool surface
- Itching or irritation around the anus
- A visible tear or skin tag near the anal opening
- Fear or anxiety about the next bowel movement

---

## Causes and Risk Factors

- Chronic constipation and passing hard stools
- Chronic diarrhoea
- Anal spasm (tight anal sphincter)
- Childbirth (especially after prolonged labour)
- Anal intercourse

High-fibre foods (fruits, vegetables, whole grains, pulses), adequate water, and avoiding highly spicy or constipating foods during recovery.

**URL:** `/services/anorectal-care/anal-fistula/`
**Meta title:** Anal Fistula Treatment Amravati | Ksharsutra & Laser Fistula Specialist
**Meta description:** Specialist anal fistula treatment in Amravati. Ksharsutra, laser (FiLaC), and conventional options. Complex and recurrent cases welcome. MS Ayurveda surgeons.

---

## Hero

### Headline
Anal Fistula Treatment

### Alternative Names
Fistula-in-Ano | Bhagandara (Sanskrit) | Bhagandar (भगंदर)

### Sub-headline
Specialist treatment for anal fistula including complex, high, and recurrent cases. Options include Ksharsutra (classical), laser fistula treatment (FiLaC), and conventional surgery, chosen for your specific fistula anatomy.

---

## Answer-First Summary

An anal fistula is an abnormal tunnel connecting the anal canal to the skin around the anus, usually forming after a perianal abscess. Fistula does not heal on its own and requires procedural treatment. Options include Ksharsutra (a classical Ayurvedic thread-based technique with well-established outcomes), laser fistula treatment (FiLaC), and conventional surgery (fistulotomy or fistulectomy). Choice depends on the fistula's anatomy, whether it is simple or complex, and whether it involves the sphincter muscles.

---

## What Is an Anal Fistula?

An anal fistula is a small tunnel that develops between the inside of the anal canal and the skin near the anus. It typically forms after a perianal abscess (a pocket of infection) has drained, either spontaneously or surgically, leaving a persistent tract.

Fistulas are classified by their anatomy and their relationship to the anal sphincter muscles: intersphincteric, transsphincteric, suprasphincteric, and extrasphincteric. Some are simple (superficial, single tract) and others are complex (deep, multiple tracts, involving significant sphincter muscle). The classification determines the appropriate treatment approach.

---

## Symptoms

- Persistent discharge (pus, blood, or stool) from an opening near the anus
- Recurrent perianal pain, swelling, or abscess
- Skin irritation around the anus
- Fever (if abscess is present)
- Foul-smelling discharge
- Sometimes visible external opening with occasional discharge

---

## Causes

- Previous perianal abscess (most common cause)
- Crohn's disease
- Tuberculosis
- Diabetes (increases risk and complicates healing)
- HIV
- Trauma or surgery to the anal area
- Radiation therapy

---

## When to See a Specialist

- Any persistent discharge from an opening near the anus
- Recurrent perianal abscess
- Chronic perianal pain or itching
- Previously treated fistula that has recurred

Fistula does not heal on its own. Delaying treatment usually leads to worsening: more complex tracts, more sphincter involvement, and more difficult repair.

---

## Diagnosis

Diagnosis involves clinical examination, sometimes complemented by:
- Fistulography
- MRI fistulogram (particularly useful for complex or recurrent cases)
- Endoanal ultrasound (in select cases)

Accurate anatomical mapping is essential for choosing the right treatment. In complex or recurrent cases, we insist on adequate imaging before proceeding.

---

## Treatment Options at Shri Manmukund Hospital

### Ksharsutra (Classical Ayurvedic)
Involves gradual application of a medicated thread (Ksharsutra) along the fistula tract over weekly sessions. The thread progressively cuts and simultaneously heals the tract, minimising sphincter injury.

**Suitable for:** Most types of fistula, including some complex and recurrent cases.
**Advantages:** Sphincter-preserving, low recurrence when performed correctly, cost-effective, no cutting or hospitalisation for each session.
**Timeframe:** Weekly follow-up over 4 to 8 weeks typically, longer for complex cases.
**Recovery:** Normal activity throughout treatment.

Ksharsutra is one of our signature practices. Over 15 years of dedicated experience.
[Link to Ksharsutra hub]

### Laser Fistula Treatment (FiLaC)
Modern minimally invasive approach. A laser fibre is passed through the fistula tract and delivers precise energy that closes the tract from within.

**Suitable for:** Simple and select complex fistulas.
**Advantages:** Sphincter-preserving, single-session procedure, day-care.
**Recovery:** 3 to 5 days.
[Link to Laser Proctology hub]

### Conventional Surgery (Fistulotomy or Fistulectomy)
Traditional surgical opening or excision of the fistula tract.

**Suitable for:** Superficial fistulas where sphincter preservation is not a major concern.
**Considerations:** Higher risk of incontinence if significant sphincter is involved.

### Seton Placement
Used for select high or complex fistulas as a bridging technique before definitive treatment.

---

## Choice of Treatment

The right approach depends on the fistula's anatomy: which sphincter muscles it involves, whether it is simple or complex, whether it is a first-time or recurrent presentation, and your general health. We recommend the approach that best balances complete healing with sphincter preservation. This individualised choice is why our practice invests in careful preoperative evaluation.

---

## Recovery and Follow-up

Varies by treatment. Ksharsutra involves weekly OPD visits over the treatment period with normal daily activity throughout. Laser and conventional surgery require 3 to 14 days recovery depending on complexity. Follow-up continues at 1 month, 3 months, and 6 months to confirm complete healing and detect any recurrence early.

---

## Prevention

Fistula prevention centres on preventing perianal abscess, which is not always possible. General measures:
- Manage diabetes carefully
- Treat perianal infections early
- Do not delay drainage of a perianal abscess
- Manage Crohn's disease actively

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Can an anal fistula heal without surgery?**
No. Fistula tracts do not heal on their own once established. Some form of procedural treatment (Ksharsutra, laser, or surgery) is needed.

**Q: What is the best treatment for anal fistula?**
There is no single best treatment. Choice depends on your fistula's anatomy. Ksharsutra offers excellent outcomes for many cases including complex ones. Laser is excellent for select cases. Conventional surgery is appropriate for others.

**Q: Is Ksharsutra treatment painful?**
Ksharsutra application is done under local anaesthesia. Between weekly applications, patients continue normal activities with minimal discomfort. Some describe mild soreness that eases within 24 hours.

**Q: How long does Ksharsutra take?**
Typically 4 to 8 weeks for simple fistulas, longer for complex or high fistulas. Duration is monitored by weekly evaluation.

**Q: Will I be incontinent after fistula treatment?**
Modern sphincter-preserving techniques including Ksharsutra and laser have low risk of incontinence when performed correctly. Traditional fistulotomy for high or complex fistulas carries higher risk, which is why we prefer sphincter-preserving approaches wherever possible.

**Q: My fistula has recurred after previous surgery. Can it still be treated?**
Yes. Recurrent fistulas are a significant part of our practice. Adequate imaging and careful planning are essential.

**Q: What is the difference between fistula and piles?**
Piles are swollen veins in the anal canal. Fistula is an abnormal tunnel between the anal canal and the skin. They are different conditions but can co-exist.

**Q: Does fistula turn into cancer?**
Long-standing untreated fistulas carry a small increased risk of certain cancers, though this is uncommon. This is another reason not to delay treatment.

**Q: What tests do I need before fistula treatment?**
Basic blood tests, sometimes screening for diabetes, and imaging (fistulogram or MRI) especially for complex or recurrent cases.

**Q: Can I work during Ksharsutra treatment?**
Yes. Normal daily activity is possible throughout Ksharsutra treatment. Only weekly OPD visits are needed.

A recurrent anal fistula is one that returns after previous treatment. Recurrence is often due to missed tracts, inadequate initial evaluation, or inappropriate technique choice for the fistula's anatomy. Successful treatment of recurrent fistula depends on thorough re-evaluation (usually with MRI fistulogram), careful mapping of all tracts, and selection of the right technique, which in most cases is Ksharsutra or laser to preserve sphincter function.

---

## Why Fistulas Recur

Recurrence usually happens for one of several reasons:

- **Missed secondary tracts** during original treatment
- **Inadequate imaging** before original procedure
- **Inappropriate technique choice** for the fistula's anatomy
- **Incomplete healing** and premature discharge
- **Underlying conditions** (Crohn's disease, tuberculosis, diabetes) that were not addressed
- **Very complex initial fistula** requiring staged treatment

Understanding why the previous treatment failed is essential to succeeding this time.

---

## Our Approach to Recurrent Cases

### Comprehensive Re-evaluation
- Detailed history including operative notes from previous surgery
- Physical examination
- Imaging: MRI fistulogram is often essential to map all tracts accurately

### Individualised Treatment Plan
Based on the current anatomy (which may differ from before because of previous surgery), we recommend one of:
- Ksharsutra (frequently the technique of choice for recurrent cases, given its sphincter preservation)
- **IFTAK (Interception of Fistula Tract And Ksharsutra):** a specialised technique used specifically in recurrent fistula to reduce total treatment duration, improve patient adherence, and minimise tissue injury. Particularly valuable when weekly visits over many weeks are difficult
- Partial Fistulectomy with Ksharsutra Ligation
- Laser fistula treatment (FiLaC)
- Staged approach (seton followed by definitive treatment)
- Occasionally conventional surgery

### Realistic Expectations
Recurrent fistula treatment has slightly higher recurrence rates than first-time treatment. We explain this honestly. Our approach maximises the probability of complete healing while preserving function.

---

## When to Consider a Second Opinion

If you have had any of these experiences:
- Fistula recurrence after previous surgery
- Persistent discharge despite treatment
- Multiple external openings
- Told your case is "too complex" or "not treatable"
- Concerns about incontinence risk from recommended surgery
- Long-standing fistula that has never fully healed

A second opinion is worthwhile. Bring:
- All previous operative reports and discharge summaries
- Any imaging done (fistulogram, MRI)
- Current medications
- Diabetes status if applicable

---

# 10. Perianal Abscess

**URL:** `/services/anorectal-care/perianal-abscess/`
**Meta title:** Perianal Abscess Treatment Amravati | Emergency Drainage & Care
**Meta description:** Timely treatment of perianal abscess in Amravati. Drainage, antibiotic care, and follow-up to prevent fistula formation. Emergency care available.

---

## Hero

### Headline
Perianal Abscess Treatment

### Alternative Names
Anal Abscess | Perianal Fistula-precursor

### Sub-headline
Timely drainage and care of perianal abscess to relieve pain, control infection, and reduce the risk of fistula formation.

---

## Answer-First Summary

A perianal abscess is a pocket of infection near the anus, causing severe pain, swelling, redness, and sometimes fever. It requires prompt drainage, usually as a minor procedure. Antibiotics alone are not sufficient. After drainage, approximately half of patients develop an anal fistula that will need separate treatment. Structured follow-up is important.

---

## What Is a Perianal Abscess?

A perianal abscess is a localised collection of pus in the tissues around the anus, usually resulting from infection of the small anal glands that normally lubricate the anal canal. When these glands become blocked and infected, pus builds up, causing severe pain and swelling.

---

## Symptoms

- Severe throbbing pain around the anus, worse with sitting, walking, or bowel movement
- Visible swelling and redness
- Warmth over the swollen area
- Fever and general unwellness
- Difficulty passing stool due to pain
- Sometimes discharge if the abscess starts to drain spontaneously

Symptoms usually develop over 1 to 3 days and worsen rapidly.

---

## Causes and Risk Factors

- Infection of anal glands (most common)
- Anal fissure with secondary infection
- Diabetes
- Immunocompromise (HIV, chemotherapy)
- Crohn's disease
- Inflammatory bowel disease
- Trauma

---

## When to See a Specialist

**Immediately**, if you have:
- Severe perianal pain with visible swelling
- Fever with perianal pain
- Rapidly worsening pain
- Discharge from a perianal opening
- Any of the above with diabetes

Perianal abscess is a condition that should not be delayed. Untreated abscess can spread, cause severe systemic infection, and lead to more complex fistula.

---

## Diagnosis

Diagnosis is usually clinical. Occasionally imaging (ultrasound or MRI) is needed to assess deep or complex abscesses.

---

## Treatment

### Incision and Drainage
The primary treatment. A small incision is made under local or short general anaesthesia to drain the pus, followed by dressing and antibiotic cover.

### Follow-up Care
Regular dressing changes, oral antibiotics, sitz baths, and pain management. Diabetic control is essential where applicable.

### Simultaneous Fistula Management
Because perianal abscess is very often associated with an underlying anal fistula, we assess for fistula at the time of abscess presentation. When both are identified, we treat them simultaneously rather than requiring a separate second procedure later. This reduces the total number of procedures the patient undergoes and shortens overall recovery. About 40 to 50% of perianal abscesses are associated with, or subsequently develop into, anal fistula, so structured follow-up over 6 to 12 weeks is also important where simultaneous treatment is not appropriate.

---

## Recovery

Most patients feel dramatically better within hours of drainage. Full recovery takes 1 to 2 weeks. Return to work is usually possible within a few days depending on job type.

---

## Prevention

- Manage diabetes carefully
- Treat anal fissure and other perianal conditions early
- Maintain good perianal hygiene
- Address chronic diarrhoea

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Will antibiotics alone treat a perianal abscess?**
No. Once an abscess is formed, drainage is essential. Antibiotics are supportive.

**Q: Is perianal abscess drainage painful?**
The drainage is done under anaesthesia. Post-drainage discomfort is significantly less than the pre-drainage abscess pain.

**Q: Will I get a fistula after abscess drainage?**
Approximately 40 to 50% of patients develop an anal fistula in the weeks following abscess drainage. Follow-up is important.

**Q: Can perianal abscess recur?**
Yes, particularly if underlying causes (fistula, diabetes, Crohn's disease) are not addressed.

**Q: Is perianal abscess dangerous?**
Untreated, it can spread to deep tissues and cause serious systemic infection. Timely drainage is important.

---

# 11. Pilonidal Sinus

**URL:** `/services/anorectal-care/pilonidal-sinus/`
**Meta title:** Pilonidal Sinus Treatment Amravati | Laser & Ksharsutra Options
**Meta description:** Specialist pilonidal sinus treatment in Amravati. Laser (SiLaC), Ksharsutra, and conventional surgical options. Recurrent cases welcome.

---

## Hero

### Headline
Pilonidal Sinus Treatment

### Sub-headline
Effective treatment for pilonidal sinus disease with options including laser (SiLaC), Ksharsutra, and conventional surgery. Recurrent cases welcome.

---

## Answer-First Summary

Pilonidal sinus is a small tunnel or cyst that develops in the natal cleft (area at the top of the buttocks), containing hair, skin debris, and sometimes infection. It causes recurrent pain, swelling, and discharge. Treatment options range from conservative measures for early cases to laser pilonidal sinus treatment (SiLaC), Ksharsutra, and various surgical excision techniques for advanced cases. Recurrence is a common problem and technique choice matters.

---

## What Is Pilonidal Sinus?

Pilonidal sinus is a chronic skin condition in the cleft between the buttocks, characterised by one or more small openings (sinuses) that often contain hair. It typically develops between ages 15 and 40 and is more common in men than women.

---

## Symptoms

- Small pit or opening at the top of the buttock cleft
- Recurrent pain and swelling in the area
- Discharge (pus, blood, or foul-smelling fluid)
- Recurrent abscess formation
- Sometimes multiple openings visible

---

## Causes and Risk Factors

- Ingrown hairs
- Prolonged sitting (drivers, office workers, students)
- Obesity
- Excessive body hair, coarse hair
- Poor hygiene in the natal cleft area
- Family history
- Age 15 to 40

---

## Treatment Options at Shri Manmukund Hospital

### Conservative Management
For early asymptomatic cases: hygiene, hair removal in the area, avoiding prolonged sitting where possible.

### Incision and Drainage
For acute abscess. Immediate relief. Usually not definitive.

### Laser Pilonidal Sinus Treatment (SiLaC)
Modern minimally invasive approach using a laser fibre through the sinus tract. Sphincter-preserving equivalent for pilonidal disease.
**Advantages:** Small incision, faster recovery, lower recurrence in appropriate cases.

### Ksharsutra
Classical Ayurvedic approach adapted for pilonidal sinus. Suitable for select cases, particularly recurrent ones.

### Conventional Surgery
Various techniques: wide excision with primary closure, excision with flap reconstruction (Karydakis, Limberg), or open granulation. Choice depends on the disease extent.

---

## Recovery

Varies by treatment. Laser: 1 to 2 weeks. Surgical excision: 2 to 6 weeks depending on technique and healing.

---

## Prevention of Recurrence

- Regular hygiene of the area
- Hair removal in the natal cleft (shaving, laser hair removal)
- Weight management
- Avoiding prolonged sitting where possible

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Can pilonidal sinus heal on its own?**
Rarely. Most cases require treatment, and untreated pilonidal sinus tends to cause recurrent infections.

**Q: Is pilonidal sinus contagious?**
No.

**Q: Is laser treatment for pilonidal sinus painful?**
Post-procedure pain is generally mild and managed with medication. Significantly less than open surgical excision.

**Q: What is the recurrence rate?**
Recurrence depends on technique, patient factors, and post-treatment care. Careful technique choice and consistent aftercare reduce recurrence.

**Q: Can pilonidal sinus become cancerous?**
Very rarely, long-standing untreated pilonidal disease has been associated with squamous cell carcinoma. Prompt treatment prevents this.

---

# 12. Rectal Prolapse

**URL:** `/services/anorectal-care/rectal-prolapse/`
**Meta title:** Rectal Prolapse Treatment Amravati | Full & Partial Prolapse Specialist
**Meta description:** Specialist evaluation and treatment for rectal prolapse in Amravati. Conservative, minimally invasive, and surgical options based on prolapse type and patient factors.

---

## Hero

### Headline
Rectal Prolapse Treatment

### Alternative Names
Guda Bhramsha (Sanskrit)

### Sub-headline
Evaluation and treatment of partial and complete rectal prolapse in adults and children, with treatment matched to prolapse type, severity, and patient factors.

---

## Answer-First Summary

Rectal prolapse is a condition where the rectum protrudes through the anus. It can be partial (mucosal only) or complete (full-thickness rectal wall). Mild cases in children often resolve with conservative management. In adults, complete prolapse usually requires surgery, with several techniques available depending on the patient's age, general health, and prolapse features.

---

## What Is Rectal Prolapse?

Rectal prolapse occurs when the rectum turns inside out and protrudes through the anal opening. It ranges from a small amount of tissue visible after straining to a large segment of rectum permanently outside the anus.

Types:
- **Mucosal prolapse:** Only the lining protrudes.
- **Complete prolapse:** Full thickness of rectum protrudes.
- **Internal prolapse (intussusception):** Rectum telescopes inside itself without external protrusion.

---

## Symptoms

- Tissue visibly protruding through the anus, initially with straining and later at rest
- Feeling of incomplete evacuation
- Mucus discharge
- Bleeding from the exposed rectal surface
- Incontinence of stool or gas
- Constipation
- Discomfort during walking or sitting

---

## Causes and Risk Factors

- Chronic straining (constipation, difficulty passing stool)
- Weakness of pelvic floor muscles (childbirth, ageing)
- Chronic cough
- Prior anorectal surgery
- Neurological conditions
- Malnutrition (particularly in children)

---

## Diagnosis

Clinical examination is often sufficient. Additional evaluation may include defaecography, anal manometry, and colonoscopy depending on the patient's age and presentation.

---

## Treatment Options

### Conservative Management (Children and Mild Adult Cases)
- Correction of constipation and straining
- Nutrition improvement
- Toilet training in children
- Pelvic floor exercises in adults

### Surgical Treatment (Most Adult Cases with Complete Prolapse)
Various techniques, chosen based on patient factors:
- Abdominal rectopexy (preferred for younger, fitter patients)
- Perineal procedures (Delorme, Altemeier) for older or higher-risk patients
- Modifications based on individual case

Choice of surgical approach is a specialist decision based on the patient's age, general health, prolapse features, and functional status.

---

## Recovery

Varies by procedure. Abdominal procedures: 2 to 4 weeks recovery. Perineal procedures: 1 to 3 weeks.

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Can rectal prolapse be cured without surgery?**
Mild prolapse in children often resolves with conservative management. Complete prolapse in adults usually requires surgery for lasting resolution.

**Q: Is rectal prolapse dangerous?**
Prolonged prolapse can cause ulceration, bleeding, and rarely strangulation. It also significantly impacts quality of life. Timely treatment is recommended.

**Q: Will surgery restore normal function?**
Most patients experience significant improvement in prolapse and often in continence. Some functional issues may persist depending on the duration of prolapse.

**Q: Can rectal prolapse recur?**
Recurrence rates vary by technique. Adequate surgical repair and correction of contributing factors (straining, chronic cough) reduce recurrence.

---

- Chronic straining (constipation, difficulty passing stool)
- Weakness of pelvic floor muscles (childbirth, ageing)
- Chronic cough
- Prior anorectal surgery
- Neurological conditions
- Malnutrition (particularly in children)

---

## Diagnosis

Clinical examination is often sufficient. Additional evaluation may include defaecography, anal manometry, and colonoscopy depending on the patient's age and presentation.

---

## Treatment Options

### Conservative Management (Children and Mild Adult Cases)
- Correction of constipation and straining
- Nutrition improvement
- Toilet training in children
- Pelvic floor exercises in adults

### Surgical Treatment (Most Adult Cases with Complete Prolapse)
Various techniques, chosen based on patient factors:
- Abdominal rectopexy (preferred for younger, fitter patients)
- Perineal procedures (Delorme, Altemeier) for older or higher-risk patients
- Modifications based on individual case

Choice of surgical approach is a specialist decision based on the patient's age, general health, prolapse features, and functional status.

---

## Recovery

Varies by procedure. Abdominal procedures: 2 to 4 weeks recovery. Perineal procedures: 1 to 3 weeks.

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Can rectal prolapse be cured without surgery?**
Mild prolapse in children often resolves with conservative management. Complete prolapse in adults usually requires surgery for lasting resolution.

**Q: Is rectal prolapse dangerous?**
Prolonged prolapse can cause ulceration, bleeding, and rarely strangulation. It also significantly impacts quality of life. Timely treatment is recommended.

**Q: Will surgery restore normal function?**
Most patients experience significant improvement in prolapse and often in continence. Some functional issues may persist depending on the duration of prolapse.

**Q: Can rectal prolapse recur?**
Recurrence rates vary by technique. Adequate surgical repair and correction of contributing factors (straining, chronic cough) reduce recurrence.

---

# 14. Ksharsutra Hub (Classical Signature Practice)

**URL:** `/services/ksharsutra/`
**Meta title:** Ksharsutra Treatment in Amravati | Classical Ayurvedic Fistula Specialist
**Meta description:** Specialist Ksharsutra treatment in Amravati. Over 15 years of dedicated practice. For anal fistula, complex cases, and select anorectal conditions.

---

## Hero

### Headline
Ksharsutra: Our Classical Ayurvedic Surgical Signature

### Sub-headline
Over 15 years of dedicated Ksharsutra practice. A sphincter-preserving classical Ayurvedic technique with well-established outcomes for anal fistula, particularly complex, high, and recurrent cases.

### Primary CTA
Book Consultation

### Secondary CTA
Call 8208927917

---

## Answer-First Summary

Ksharsutra is a classical Ayurvedic parasurgical technique that uses a medicated thread to gradually treat anal fistula and select other anorectal conditions. The thread simultaneously cuts and heals the tract over weekly sessions, minimising injury to the sphincter muscles. Ksharsutra is particularly valuable for complex, high, and recurrent fistulas where sphincter preservation is critical. Dr. Vipin Tongale at Shri Manmukund Hospital has practised Ksharsutra for over 15 years across multiple institutions.

---

## What is Ksharsutra?

Ksharsutra is described in the classical Ayurvedic surgical text Sushruta Samhita, composed over two millennia ago. The technique uses a medicated thread coated with alkaline substances (Kshara, prepared from Achyranthes aspera and other classical Ayurvedic ingredients). The thread is applied through the fistula tract and changed at weekly intervals.

Each thread change progressively:
- Debrides unhealthy tissue lining the tract
- Applies medicated alkali to the tract wall
- Physically cuts through remaining tract with minimal collateral injury
- Simultaneously stimulates healing of the tissue behind it

The result is gradual healing of the fistula tract from inside out, with the sphincter muscles preserved to the maximum possible extent.

---

## Why Ksharsutra Matters

Anal fistula treatment has a fundamental problem: the tract often passes through or near the anal sphincter muscles that maintain continence. Aggressive surgical cutting risks incontinence. Conservative approaches often leave residual disease that recurs.

Ksharsutra offers a middle path. The gradual cutting-and-healing action of the medicated thread substantially reduces the incontinence risk associated with aggressive fistulotomy while providing definitive treatment of the tract. For complex or high fistulas, this sphincter-preserving property is not just an advantage; it is often the deciding factor.

---

## Conditions Treated

**Anal Fistula** (primary indication)
- Simple fistula
- Complex or multi-tract fistula
- High transsphincteric fistula
- Recurrent fistula after previous surgery

**Selected other anorectal conditions**
- Internal piles (via Ksharkarma application)
- Piles associated with fistula or fissure
- Pilonidal sinus (in select cases)
- Certain chronic anorectal wounds

---

## Specialised Ksharsutra Techniques We Offer

**Classical Ksharsutra:** medicated thread application through the fistula tract, changed weekly until healing is complete.

**Partial Fistulectomy with Ksharsutra Ligation:** a hybrid technique where the superficial or accessible portion of the fistula tract is surgically excised while Ksharsutra is applied to the deeper tract that involves the sphincter. This reduces overall treatment duration while preserving the sphincter-sparing advantage of Ksharsutra for the critical portion.

**IFTAK (Interception of Fistula Tract And Ksharsutra):** a specialised technique used for select complex and recurrent fistulas. IFTAK reduces overall treatment duration, improves patient adherence (fewer weekly visits over a shorter period), and minimises tissue injury compared to classical Ksharsutra alone. Particularly valuable for patients travelling from a distance where weekly visits over many weeks are impractical.

**Ksharkarma for internal piles:** application of medicated Kshara to internal haemorrhoidal tissue for controlled resolution. A non-cutting technique suitable for select cases.

---

## Sub-Pages Within This Hub
- Ksharsutra for Anal Fistula: Detailed Clinical Guide
- Ksharsutra Procedure and Recovery: What to Expect Week by Week
- Ksharkarma: The Related Ayurvedic Caustic Technique

---

## Our Ksharsutra Experience

Dr. Vipin Tongale has practised Ksharsutra for over 15 years across three institutions: Shri Gurudev Ayurved Mahavidyalaya (Mozari), District Hospital Amravati (under AYUSH ministry), and Shri Manmukund Hospital. Dr. Swati Tongale also trained in Ksharsutra during her MS Ayurveda Shalya Tantra and offers it for female patients under female-specialist care.

This experience matters. Ksharsutra outcomes depend significantly on:
- Correct case selection (which fistulas suit Ksharsutra, which do not)
- Accurate mapping of the tract
- Proper thread preparation
- Consistent application technique
- Structured follow-up

Our contribution to Ksharsutra literature and practice reflects a specialist commitment to this modality beyond routine use.

---

## When Ksharsutra is Our Preferred Recommendation

- Transsphincteric or higher fistula where sphincter preservation is critical
- Recurrent fistula after previous surgery
- Complex fistula with multiple tracts
- Patients wanting to avoid conventional surgical excision
- Patients unwilling to accept the incontinence risk of extensive fistulotomy

---

## When Alternatives May Be Better

We recommend other approaches for:
- Very superficial subcutaneous fistula (often suits laser or minor surgery)
- Fistula with active inflammatory bowel disease requiring different approach
- Cases where the tract cannot be traversed by thread
- Patient preferences for single-session procedures (Ksharsutra requires weekly visits over weeks)

Honest recommendation matters more than technique loyalty.

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Is Ksharsutra painful?**
Ksharsutra application is performed under local anaesthesia. Between weekly applications, most patients experience mild soreness for 24 hours, then normal comfort.

**Q: How long does Ksharsutra treatment take?**
Simple fistulas typically take 4 to 8 weeks. Complex or high fistulas may take longer. Duration is assessed weekly.

**Q: Can I work during Ksharsutra treatment?**
Yes. Normal daily activity is possible throughout. Only weekly OPD visits are needed.

**Q: Is Ksharsutra a proven technique?**
Yes. Ksharsutra has substantial clinical literature and is recognised by AYUSH and standard Ayurvedic surgical practice.

**Q: Will I be incontinent after Ksharsutra?**
Ksharsutra is designed specifically for sphincter preservation. Incontinence risk is significantly lower than aggressive surgical fistulotomy, especially for high or complex fistulas.

**Q: How does Ksharsutra compare with laser?**
Both are sphincter-preserving. Laser is single-session with faster completion typically. Ksharsutra takes weeks but has stronger evidence for complex and recurrent cases. Choice depends on your fistula. See our full comparison guide.

**Q: Can Ksharsutra treat piles?**
Yes, particularly piles associated with fistula or fissure. For isolated piles without associated conditions, other options may be equally or more suitable.

**Q: What is the cost of Ksharsutra treatment?**
Cost varies by complexity and duration. Please call 8208927917 for current guidance.

---

The classical Ayurvedic technique for sphincter-preserving fistula treatment, including complex, high, and recurrent cases.

---

## Answer-First Summary

Ksharsutra is a first-line consideration for anal fistula treatment where sphincter preservation matters, particularly for complex, high transsphincteric, or recurrent fistulas. A medicated Ayurvedic thread is applied through the tract and changed weekly over 4 to 12 weeks (depending on complexity), gradually healing the fistula from inside out. Success rates are high in appropriately selected cases, and incontinence risk is significantly lower than aggressive fistulotomy.

---

## How Ksharsutra Works for Fistula

The fistula tract is first identified and its full length assessed. A specially prepared Ayurvedic medicated thread is then passed through the tract, tied loosely, and left in place for one week.

Over the week, the alkaline medications on the thread:
1. Debride necrotic and unhealthy tissue lining the tract
2. Stimulate healthy granulation from the base
3. Progressively narrow the tract wall through controlled tissue action

At each weekly visit, the thread is tightened or replaced. Over successive weeks, the tract shortens and heals from the inside out. When the tract has fully healed and the thread cuts through, treatment is complete.

The sphincter muscles, which the fistula passes through or near, are preserved throughout because the gradual controlled action does not cause the abrupt injury of surgical division.

---

## Ksharsutra vs Fistulotomy

Conventional fistulotomy involves cutting open the fistula tract, dividing whatever tissue lies in the way including sphincter muscle. This works well for superficial fistulas but carries significant incontinence risk for high or complex fistulas.

Ksharsutra preserves sphincter integrity by progressive gradual action instead of one-time cutting. This is particularly valuable for:
- Transsphincteric fistula
- Suprasphincteric fistula
- Multiple-tract complex fistula
- Recurrent fistula after previous surgery

---

## Success Rates and Realistic Expectations

Ksharsutra has high success rates in appropriately selected fistula cases when performed by experienced practitioners. Complete healing is expected in the majority of cases. Recurrence rates are comparable to or lower than surgical alternatives, particularly for complex cases.

We are honest about limits:
- Very complex cases may require staged treatment
- Some cases benefit from initial imaging before Ksharsutra begins
- Underlying conditions (Crohn's disease, tuberculosis, diabetes) affect outcomes and must be addressed alongside
- No technique offers 100% success

---

## Case Selection

Not every fistula is best treated with Ksharsutra. Our consultation includes:
- Detailed history including any previous treatments
- Examination
- Imaging (MRI fistulogram) for complex or recurrent cases
- Assessment of underlying conditions
- Discussion of all appropriate options (Ksharsutra, laser, conventional surgery)

We recommend Ksharsutra when it is genuinely the best option for your case. If another approach fits better, we recommend that.

---

## What to Expect

**First Visit:** consultation, examination, discussion of options, preoperative evaluation.

**Ksharsutra Application:** performed under local anaesthesia in the OT, typically 20 to 45 minutes, same-day discharge.

**Weekly Sessions:** brief OPD visit, thread tightened or replaced, progress assessed.

**Completion:** confirmed healing, follow-up at 3 months and 6 months to detect any recurrence early.

---

# 16. Ksharsutra Procedure and Recovery Guide

**URL:** `/services/ksharsutra/procedure-and-recovery/`
**Meta title:** Ksharsutra Procedure and Recovery Guide | What to Expect | Amravati
**Meta description:** Complete guide to Ksharsutra procedure and recovery. Day-by-day expectations, aftercare, and practical guidance for patients considering or undergoing treatment.

---

## Hero

### Headline
Ksharsutra Procedure and Recovery: A Practical Guide

### Sub-headline
What to expect from the first visit through complete healing. Written for patients considering or currently undergoing Ksharsutra treatment.

---

## Answer-First Summary

Ksharsutra treatment involves an initial thread application under local anaesthesia (day-care procedure) followed by weekly OPD visits over 4 to 12 weeks. Between visits, patients maintain normal activities with basic aftercare (sitz baths, diet, hygiene). Discomfort is mild and manageable. Full recovery follows the last thread change once complete tract healing is confirmed.

---

## Before Your First Visit

**Bring:**
- Any previous medical records, operative notes, or imaging
- List of current medications
- A companion for the day of procedure if you wish

**Preoperative Evaluation:**
- Blood tests (haemoglobin, blood sugar, coagulation profile)
- Imaging (fistulogram or MRI) if complex or recurrent
- General health assessment

---

## Day of Application

**Timing:** usually morning slot
**Duration:** 30 to 60 minutes including preparation
**Anaesthesia:** local anaesthesia; occasionally short spinal for complex cases
**Discharge:** same day, typically within 2 to 4 hours after the procedure

**During procedure:**
- The tract is identified and cleaned
- The medicated Ksharsutra thread is passed through
- Thread is tied loosely
- A small dressing is applied

**After procedure:**
- You will feel some soreness, generally mild
- Rest at home for the rest of the day
- Take prescribed medications as directed
- Sitz baths begin from the next day

---

## Week 1 Between First and Second Visit

**Comfort:**
- Mild soreness for the first 24 to 48 hours
- Some discharge from the tract is normal (part of the healing process)
- Discomfort usually eases significantly by day 3

**Care:**
- Warm sitz baths 2 to 3 times daily
- Keep the perianal area clean and dry
- High-fibre diet, adequate fluids
- Stool softener if constipated
- Avoid heavy lifting

**Return to work:**
- Desk jobs: 1 to 2 days
- Physical jobs: 3 to 5 days

---

## Weekly OPD Visits

Each weekly visit takes 10 to 20 minutes. The doctor:
- Inspects the tract and thread
- Tightens or replaces the thread as needed
- Assesses healing progress
- Answers your questions

Between visits, continue normal activities and aftercare.

---

## Signs of Normal Healing
- Gradual reduction in discharge
- Reduction in tract length week over week
- No new external openings
- No fever or spreading redness

---

## When to Contact Us Immediately
- Heavy bleeding
- Severe unrelenting pain
- Fever above 100.4°F / 38°C
- Rapidly spreading redness or swelling
- Any new opening or discharge point

Emergency line: 9405404492 (24 hours)

---

## Completion

When the tract has healed completely and the thread has fallen away, treatment is complete. A final examination confirms healing. Follow-up appointments at 3 months and 6 months monitor for any recurrence.

---

## Diet and Lifestyle During Treatment

**Include:** high-fibre foods, adequate fluids (2 to 3 litres daily), regular light physical activity (walking).

**Avoid:** very spicy foods, excess alcohol, prolonged sitting, straining during defecation.

---

## After Complete Healing

- Continue high-fibre diet and adequate fluids
- Manage any underlying conditions (diabetes, IBD, chronic diarrhoea)
- Report any new symptoms promptly
- Attend scheduled follow-up

---

**URL:** `/services/ksharkarma/`

## Hero

### Headline
Ksharkarma: Classical Ayurvedic Caustic Therapy

### Sub-headline
Non-cutting Ayurvedic parasurgical technique using medicated caustic paste. Suitable for chronic anal fissure and select other conditions.

---

## Answer-First Summary

Ksharkarma is a classical Ayurvedic parasurgical technique that applies a medicated alkaline (Kshara) paste directly to pathological tissue, achieving controlled chemical cauterisation. It differs from Ksharsutra (which uses a thread) and is particularly useful for chronic anal fissure and select anorectal conditions where a non-cutting approach is preferred.

---

## What is Ksharkarma?

Ksharkarma involves the direct application of a specially prepared Kshara (alkaline) paste to the target tissue. The Kshara acts by controlled tissue destruction and simultaneous stimulation of healing. The technique is described in Sushruta Samhita alongside Ksharsutra as one of the classical Ayurvedic parasurgical approaches.

Ksharkarma differs from Ksharsutra:
- **Ksharkarma:** paste applied to tissue (single or few applications)
- **Ksharsutra:** medicated thread applied through a tract (weekly for weeks)

Both use Kshara. Different indications, different techniques.

---

## Conditions Treated
- Internal piles (haemorrhoids): primary indication at our hospital
- Selected superficial anorectal conditions
- Select cases where surgical excision is undesirable

**Note on anal fissure:** Ksharkarma is described in classical texts for anorectal indications but we do not use it for anal fissure because it is a painful procedure in that location. For chronic fissure not responding to conservative treatment, we prefer Matra Basti with Ayurvedic medication.

---

## How the Procedure Works
- The target tissue is identified during examination
- Adjacent healthy tissue is protected
- The prepared Kshara paste is applied for a controlled time
- After the specified action time, the Kshara is neutralised and washed off
- The area heals over subsequent days with structured aftercare

---

## Advantages
- Non-cutting technique
- Preserves surrounding tissue
- Day-care procedure
- Suitable for patients wanting to avoid formal surgery
- Rooted in centuries-old Ayurvedic surgical practice

---

## When Ksharkarma is Preferred
- Chronic anal fissure resistant to conservative treatment
- Selected patients preferring Ayurvedic non-cutting approach
- Cases where laser or conventional surgery is unsuitable

---

## When Alternatives May Be Better
- Acute anal fissure (conservative treatment first)
- Cases requiring precise tissue division
- Very extensive disease

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Is Ksharkarma the same as Ksharsutra?**
No. Both use Kshara but differ in technique. Ksharkarma is caustic paste application. Ksharsutra is a medicated thread applied through a tract.

**Q: Is Ksharkarma painful?**
Performed under local anaesthesia. Post-procedure discomfort is mild.

**Q: How long is recovery?**
Typically 5 to 10 days for full healing.

---
