## Hero

### Headline
Why I Chose Shalya Tantra Over Modern Surgery Alone

### Author byline
By Dr. Vipin Tongale, MS Ayurveda Shalya Tantra, PhD

---

## Introduction

When I tell people I am an MS in Ayurveda Shalya Tantra, they sometimes ask why I did not "just do MBBS and MS General Surgery." The question implies a hierarchy: modern surgery at the top, Ayurvedic surgery somewhere below. In this piece I want to explain why that hierarchy is misplaced, and why my choice was deliberate rather than compromised.

---

## What Shalya Tantra Actually Is

Shalya Tantra is one of the eight classical branches of Ayurveda. Its foundational text is Sushruta Samhita, composed over two thousand years ago. Sushruta describes surgical instruments, procedures, anaesthesia, wound management, and post-operative care with remarkable systematic detail. He is often referred to as the father of surgery.

The modern MS Ayurveda Shalya Tantra programme is a three-year postgraduate degree that combines classical Ayurvedic surgical training with substantial exposure to modern surgical principles, anatomy, pharmacology, and clinical practice. Graduates practise as surgeons in general surgical conditions with particular expertise in anorectal work, Ksharsutra, Uttarbasti, and classical Ayurvedic surgical techniques.

---

## Why I Chose This Path

I could give a philosophical answer about respecting tradition, but that would be incomplete.

The practical answer is this: as an anorectal specialist, my patients need both classical Ayurvedic tools (Ksharsutra, Ksharkarma, Uttarbasti, Panchakarma) and modern surgical tools (laser, minimally invasive techniques, modern wound management). A patient with a complex recurrent fistula may be best served by Ksharsutra. Another patient with simple Grade II piles may be best served by laser or a non-surgical procedure. A patient with a stricture urethra may benefit from Uttarbasti. A patient with an acute abscess needs immediate drainage.

Shalya Tantra training gave me competence in all of these. The alternative, training as an allopathic general surgeon, would have given me competence in modern techniques but no formal training in classical Ayurvedic ones. I would then either have to add Ayurvedic techniques informally, which is not the same as postgraduate training, or refer patients away for classical treatment.

The choice was not compromise. It was optimisation.

---

## What This Means for Patients

If your case is best treated by a classical Ayurvedic technique, I can offer it competently. If your case is best treated by a modern technique, I can offer that too, or coordinate with expert visiting specialists for procedures beyond my direct scope (like laparoscopic cholecystectomy).

The important thing is that the recommendation to you is honest, based on what your case needs, not what my training happens to include.

This is why I have deliberately built a practice that offers Ksharsutra, laser, non-surgical, and conventional options, and why I recommend the one that fits your case rather than defaulting to whichever I have most invested in.

---

## The Broader Point

There is a false framing in India that pits modern medicine against Ayurveda as if they are competitors. In practice, the frame is unhelpful for patients. What patients need is honest evaluation and appropriate treatment. Sometimes that is modern medicine. Sometimes that is Ayurveda. Sometimes that is both, coordinated.

Doctors trained only in one tradition often struggle with this because their instinct is to recommend within their scope. Doctors trained in both, or willing to work with both honestly, can serve patients better.

My choice of Shalya Tantra was, in this sense, a choice about the kind of doctor I wanted to be for my patients. I do not regret it.

---

## What Has Not Changed

Fifteen years, sixteen thousand surgeries, one PhD, and a hospital later, my core belief is unchanged: the right treatment for the patient in front of you is the right treatment, regardless of whether the framework is classical or modern.

I would like to see Indian medicine move in the direction of that pragmatism. Fewer camps. Fewer identity politics between systems. More honest care.

---

**Author Byline (full)**

Dr. Vipin Tongale is co-founder of Shri Manmukund Hospital, Amravati, and Assistant Professor of Shalya Tantra (formerly at Mahatma Gandhi Ayurved College, Salod, and Vidarbha Ayurved Mahavidyalaya, Amravati). He completed his MS in Ayurveda Shalya Tantra (2010) and PhD (2024) from Government Ayurved College, Nanded. His PhD research examined the safety and efficacy of Apamarga Kshara ointment in internal haemorrhoids management.

Fifteen years, sixteen thousand surgeries, one PhD, and a hospital later, my core belief is unchanged: the right treatment for the patient in front of you is the right treatment, regardless of whether the framework is classical or modern.

I would like to see Indian medicine move in the direction of that pragmatism. Fewer camps. Fewer identity politics between systems. More honest care.

---

**Author Byline (full)**

Dr. Vipin Tongale is co-founder of Shri Manmukund Hospital, Amravati, and Assistant Professor of Shalya Tantra (formerly at Mahatma Gandhi Ayurved College, Salod, and Vidarbha Ayurved Mahavidyalaya, Amravati). He completed his MS in Ayurveda Shalya Tantra (2010) and PhD (2024) from Government Ayurved College, Nanded. His PhD research examined the safety and efficacy of Apamarga Kshara ointment in internal haemorrhoids management.

# 82. Insights: The Case for Female Surgeons in Anorectal Practice

**URL:** `/knowledge/insights/case-for-female-surgeons-in-anorectal-practice/`
**Cluster:** Insights
**Author:** Dr. Swati Tongale (first-person)
**Meta title:** The Case for Female Surgeons in Anorectal Practice | Dr. Swati Tongale
**Meta description:** A personal reflection on why female patients deserve the choice of a female surgeon for anorectal and gynaecological care.

---

## Hero

### Headline
The Case for Female Surgeons in Anorectal Practice

### Author byline
By Dr. Swati Tongale, MS Ayurveda Shalya Tantra

---

## The Consultations I Remember

I remember a woman in her mid-forties who had been living with a painful anal fissure for three years. Three years. She had not consulted a doctor because her local specialists were all male, and the thought of examination was, in her words, "impossible to imagine." When she finally came to our hospital because someone told her there was a female surgeon, she cried in the consultation room before we even started talking.

I remember a young woman with a fistula that had progressed to complex disease over two years of avoidance. Her fistula could have been treated much more easily two years earlier.

I remember dozens of women who told me, quietly, that they had specifically requested a female specialist and were relieved to find one. Not because male specialists are bad. Because for certain examinations and procedures, patient comfort with the doctor's gender matters, and the option should exist.

---

## What This Access Barrier Actually Costs

In much of Vidarbha and rural Maharashtra, female surgeons are uncommon. Anorectal specialists specifically are even rarer to find in female form. This is not an abstract statistic; it is a lived reality that costs women health outcomes every day.

Women delay consultation for:
- Anorectal problems (piles, fissure, fistula)
- Female-specific concerns (gynaecological Ayurvedic care, Uttarbasti indications)
- Sensitive medical issues generally

The delay converts easily-treatable conditions into complex ones, and treatable conditions into chronic ones. It is a real, measurable cost.

---

## Why I Focus on Female Care

Practising as one half of a husband-wife surgical partnership at Shri Manmukund Hospital, I have deliberately built my clinical scope around this access gap. My practice includes:

- Female proctology (piles, fissure, fistula, pilonidal in women)
- Uttarbasti for infertility (a specialised Ayurvedic application)
- Menstrual disorders and postnatal Ayurvedic care
- General surgical care with a female-patient-preferred option

The intent is not to make gender central to every consultation. It is to remove gender as a barrier when it is one, and to be available as a specialist when female patients want that specifically.

---

## What Male Colleagues Get Right and What They Cannot

Male surgeons are excellent clinicians. I have learnt substantially from male teachers, colleagues, and my clinical partner Dr. Vipin. Nothing in this piece suggests otherwise.

But there are consultations, examinations, and procedures where a female patient simply prefers a female specialist. This preference is not irrational, not old-fashioned, not something patients should be pushed to overcome. It is a legitimate preference that deserves accommodation.

The best male colleagues understand this and welcome female-specialist availability as a benefit to patients. The best clinical partnerships include both genders precisely so patients have the choice.

---

## What I Would Like Female Patients to Know

If you have been delaying a consultation because your local specialist is male, please consider:

1. The problem you are avoiding is very likely treatable.
2. Delay often makes it more complex to treat, not less.
3. Female-specialist options exist. Ours is one; there are others across Maharashtra and India.
4. In the consultation, you will be treated with dignity, in privacy, at your pace.
5. A companion (mother, sister, husband, friend) is welcome to accompany you.

You have carried this concern long enough. Let a specialist help.

---

## What I Would Like Medical Systems to Do

At institutional and policy level, three things would improve female access to specialty care:

1. More female surgical trainees, especially in surgical specialties historically male-dominated.
2. Institutional recognition that female-specialist availability matters for female patient outcomes.
3. Marketing and communication from hospitals that explicitly acknowledges the female-specialist option.

None of this is anti-male. It is pro-patient. Female patients deserve the option.

---

## What I Do in My Own Practice

Every female patient who comes to Shri Manmukund Hospital is offered the option of female-specialist care. If she prefers to see Dr. Vipin, she does. If she prefers to see me, she does. If she wants a companion during examination, one is welcome. If she wants to bring her mother, sister, or husband, they are welcome.

These are small things. They add up to something larger: a practice where female patients feel comfortable seeking care they need.

That is the case for female surgeons in anorectal practice, in my words.

---

**Author Byline (full)**

Dr. Swati Tongale, MS Ayurveda Shalya Tantra, is co-founder of Shri Manmukund Hospital, Amravati, and lead of the Female Care Unit. Her clinical focus includes female proctology, Uttarbasti for infertility, menstrual disorders, and postnatal Ayurvedic care. She practices alongside her clinical partner Dr. Vipin Tongale, and specifically serves patients who prefer a female specialist for sensitive care.

---

# 84. First Visit Guide

**URL:** `/patients/first-visit/`
**Meta title:** First Visit Guide | Shri Manmukund Hospital Amravati
**Meta description:** What to expect at your first consultation at Shri Manmukund Hospital. Preparation, examination, timing, companions, and next steps.

---

## Hero

### Headline
What to Expect at Your First Consultation

### Sub-headline
Practical guidance for your first visit to Shri Manmukund Hospital. Anorectal consultations especially can feel intimidating; this guide helps you feel prepared.

---

## Answer-First Summary

Your first consultation at Shri Manmukund Hospital typically takes 30 to 45 minutes and includes detailed history-taking, physical examination, discussion of findings, and treatment options. Companions are welcome. Female patients may specifically request Dr. Swati. Bring any previous medical records. There is no need to be embarrassed; we see these conditions daily and treat every patient with dignity.

---

## Before You Come

**Book an appointment:** call 8208927917 or WhatsApp to schedule. Walk-in is also possible during OPD hours but a booked appointment reduces waiting time.

**Bring:**
- Any previous prescriptions or medical records
- List of current medications (or the medicines themselves)
- Any imaging or reports (ultrasound, MRI, CT scans, blood tests) from previous evaluations
- Aadhaar or other identity document
- Insurance card if applicable

**Wear comfortable clothing** that allows easy access to the area of concern if it will be examined.

**Do not fast** unless we specifically instruct you to. Come after a normal meal.

---

## When You Arrive

**Reception:** register at the reception desk with your name and appointment details.

**Waiting:** the waiting area is comfortable and private. Your wait time depends on the day's OPD schedule; we try to minimise it.

**Consultation:** you will be called into the doctor's consultation chamber (Dr. Vipin's or Dr. Swati's based on your preference or the appointment).

---

## What Happens in the Consultation

**Detailed history (10 to 15 minutes):**
The doctor will ask about your symptoms, when they started, how they have progressed, what treatments you have tried, your general health, medications, and any relevant family history. Please answer honestly and completely; nothing you say surprises us.

**Physical examination (5 to 10 minutes):**
For most conditions, examination includes inspection and gentle physical assessment. For anorectal conditions, this typically includes digital rectal examination and sometimes proctoscopy. The examination is uncomfortable but rarely painful. It is done in privacy with dignity maintained throughout.

**Discussion of findings (10 to 15 minutes):**
The doctor will explain what was found, what the likely diagnosis is, what investigations if any are needed, and what treatment options exist. You will have time to ask questions.

**Investigations if needed:**
Blood tests, imaging, or other investigations may be scheduled. Some can be done on-site.

**Next steps:**
Treatment plan, prescription, follow-up appointment.

---

## Bringing a Companion

You are welcome to bring a family member or friend. Many patients find it helpful to have someone present:
- During the initial discussion
- To help remember information
- For moral support

For examinations, your preference determines whether the companion is present. Female patients may specifically request Dr. Swati and may have female companions present throughout.

---

## Common Concerns

**"I am embarrassed about my symptoms."**
Every symptom you might describe is one we hear regularly. Anorectal conditions in particular are common, and we treat many patients daily. Nothing you say will surprise us or make us judge you.

**"What if I have been ignoring this for years?"**
Many patients delay for years before consulting. We do not judge. We start from where you are and plan the best way forward.

**"I do not want a male doctor to examine me."**
Female patients can specifically request Dr. Swati. Please mention this when booking.

**"What if I need surgery?"**
Not every consultation ends in a surgery recommendation. Many conditions are managed with lifestyle changes, medication, or minor procedures. If surgery is genuinely needed, we discuss the options honestly.

**"How much will this cost?"**
Consultation fees are modest. Investigation and treatment costs depend on what is needed. We discuss costs openly. Call 8208927917 for current consultation fees.

---

## After Your First Visit

Depending on findings, next steps may include:
- Scheduled investigations
- Follow-up appointment
- Starting prescribed medication
- Planning a procedure
- Referral if your case needs a different specialist

You will leave with clear next-step guidance in writing (or WhatsApp).

---

## Contact
Appointment: 8208927917 | Emergency: 9405404492 | WhatsApp

# 85. Pre-Surgery Preparation

**URL:** `/patients/pre-surgery/`
**Meta title:** Pre-Surgery Preparation Guide | Shri Manmukund Hospital
**Meta description:** Complete pre-surgery preparation guide. Fasting, medications, tests, what to pack, mental preparation. Written for our patients.

---

## Hero

### Headline
Preparing for Surgery: A Practical Guide

### Sub-headline
Everything you need to do before your procedure at Shri Manmukund Hospital. General guidance that applies to most procedures.

---

## Answer-First Summary

Pre-surgery preparation typically begins 1 to 2 weeks before your scheduled procedure. Preparation includes preoperative investigations (blood tests, ECG for older patients, imaging as needed), medication review, fasting instructions for the procedure day, and practical arrangements. Your specific procedure will have specific instructions; this guide covers the general framework.

---

## 1 to 2 Weeks Before

**Preoperative investigations:**
- Complete blood count, blood sugar, kidney function
- Coagulation profile
- HIV, HBsAg, HCV screening (standard preoperative)
- ECG if age over 40 or as clinically indicated
- Imaging specific to your case

**Medication review:**
Bring your current medication list to the pre-op consultation. Some medications need adjustment before surgery:
- Blood thinners (aspirin, clopidogrel, warfarin, new-generation blood thinners): may need pausing under supervision
- Diabetes medications: dose adjustments may be needed
- Blood pressure medications: usually continued
- Herbal supplements: some need pausing

Do not stop any medication without medical guidance.

**Lifestyle:**
- Stop smoking (ideally 4 weeks before, minimum 2 weeks)
- Reduce or stop alcohol (minimum 1 week before)
- Optimise blood sugar if diabetic
- Report any new illness (fever, cough, cold) before the procedure date

---

## The Day Before

**Diet:**
- Normal meals until instructed to fast
- Light dinner if fasting starts overnight
- Adequate hydration

**Practical:**
- Arrange transportation to and from the hospital
- Arrange a companion for the day
- Prepare a small overnight bag if admission is planned
- Confirm your reporting time with the hospital

**Rest:**
- Get adequate sleep the night before
- Avoid strenuous activity

---

## Fasting Instructions

Your specific procedure will have specific instructions. General guidelines:

**For procedures under local anaesthesia only:**
- Usually no fasting required
- Light meal a few hours before

**For procedures under spinal or general anaesthesia:**
- Nothing to eat for 6 to 8 hours before
- Clear liquids (water, clear juice) up to 2 hours before (as instructed)
- No milk, tea, coffee with milk for 6 hours before

Follow the specific fasting instructions you receive. If unclear, call us to confirm.

---

## What to Pack

**For same-day procedures:**
- Identity document
- Payment method (cash, card, insurance details)
- Comfortable loose clothing
- Slippers
- Personal medications
- Any support items (glasses, hearing aids)

**For admission (1 to 3 days):**
Add to the above:
- Sleepwear
- Toiletries
- Change of clothes
- Phone charger
- Reading material
- Snacks for after the procedure (if permitted)

---

## Mental Preparation

Anxiety before a procedure is normal. Some things that help:

**Understand what will happen.** Ask your surgeon to explain the procedure step by step until you feel informed.

**Ask about pain management.** Modern anaesthesia and pain management are effective. Understanding this reduces fear.

**Ask about recovery.** Knowing what to expect after helps reduce anxiety.

**Plan the day.** Practical planning (transport, companion, home arrangement) reduces last-minute stress.

**Sleep well the night before.** If sleep is difficult, discuss with your doctor.

---

## Reporting to the Hospital

**Reporting time:** confirm with the hospital. Usually 1 to 2 hours before the scheduled procedure time.

**Registration and preparation:**
- Reception
- Preoperative preparation in the pre-op area
- Change into hospital gown
- IV line placement if needed
- Meet the anaesthetist if applicable
- Final consultation with the surgeon
- Consent form signing

**Companion:** your companion can wait in the family waiting area. We will update them at key points.

---

## After the Procedure

Follow your specific post-procedure guidance. Refer to:
- Post-Surgery Recovery general guide
- Complete Recovery After Piles Surgery playbook (if applicable)
- Complete Recovery After Fistula Surgery playbook (if applicable)
- Ksharsutra Treatment Guide (if applicable)

---

Appointment: 8208927917 | Emergency: 9405404492 | WhatsApp

- Clear liquids (water, clear juice) up to 2 hours before (as instructed)
- No milk, tea, coffee with milk for 6 hours before

Follow the specific fasting instructions you receive. If unclear, call us to confirm.

---

## What to Pack

**For same-day procedures:**
- Identity document
- Payment method (cash, card, insurance details)
- Comfortable loose clothing
- Slippers
- Personal medications
- Any support items (glasses, hearing aids)

**For admission (1 to 3 days):**
Add to the above:
- Sleepwear
- Toiletries
- Change of clothes
- Phone charger
- Reading material
- Snacks for after the procedure (if permitted)

---

## Mental Preparation

Anxiety before a procedure is normal. Some things that help:

**Understand what will happen.** Ask your surgeon to explain the procedure step by step until you feel informed.

**Ask about pain management.** Modern anaesthesia and pain management are effective. Understanding this reduces fear.

**Ask about recovery.** Knowing what to expect after helps reduce anxiety.

**Plan the day.** Practical planning (transport, companion, home arrangement) reduces last-minute stress.

**Sleep well the night before.** If sleep is difficult, discuss with your doctor.

---

## Reporting to the Hospital

**Reporting time:** confirm with the hospital. Usually 1 to 2 hours before the scheduled procedure time.

**Registration and preparation:**
- Reception
- Preoperative preparation in the pre-op area
- Change into hospital gown
- IV line placement if needed
- Meet the anaesthetist if applicable
- Final consultation with the surgeon
- Consent form signing

**Companion:** your companion can wait in the family waiting area. We will update them at key points.

---

## After the Procedure

Follow your specific post-procedure guidance. Refer to:
- Post-Surgery Recovery general guide
- Complete Recovery After Piles Surgery playbook (if applicable)
- Complete Recovery After Fistula Surgery playbook (if applicable)
- Ksharsutra Treatment Guide (if applicable)

---

## Contact
Appointment: 8208927917 | Emergency: 9405404492 | WhatsApp

# 86. Post-Surgery Recovery (General Guide)

**URL:** `/patients/post-surgery/`
**Meta title:** Post-Surgery Recovery General Guide | Shri Manmukund Hospital
**Meta description:** General principles of post-surgery recovery. Diet, activity, wound care, medication, follow-up, and warning signs.

---

## Hero

### Headline
Post-Surgery Recovery: General Principles

### Sub-headline
General guidance for recovery after any surgery. Procedure-specific playbooks are available for anorectal procedures.

---

## Answer-First Summary

Post-surgery recovery follows predictable phases: immediate recovery (24 to 72 hours), early recovery (first week), progressive recovery (weeks 2 to 6), and long-term recovery (beyond 6 weeks). This general guide covers the principles that apply to most procedures. Procedure-specific guidance is available in dedicated playbooks.

---

## The Four Phases of Recovery

### Phase 1: Immediate Recovery (First 24 to 72 Hours)

**Priorities:**
- Rest
- Pain management with prescribed medication
- Adequate fluids
- Light meals as tolerated
- Wound care as instructed
- No driving after anaesthesia

**What is normal:**
- Some pain (managed by medication)
- Fatigue
- Mild nausea if you had general anaesthesia
- Reduced appetite

**What to report:**
- Uncontrolled pain
- High fever
- Heavy bleeding
- Persistent vomiting
- Any breathing difficulty
- Emergency: 9405404492

### Phase 2: Early Recovery (Days 4 to 7)

**Priorities:**
- Wound care continues
- Gradual return to light activity
- Diet advancing to normal
- Bowel and bladder function returning to normal

**Common concerns:**
- First bowel movement anxiety (see Piles Recovery playbook)
- Wound discharge
- Discomfort at wound site
- Fatigue

**Follow-up:**
- Day 3 or Day 7 visit as scheduled
- Photographs via WhatsApp can be sent between visits for any concerns

### Phase 3: Progressive Recovery (Weeks 2 to 6)

**Priorities:**
- Increasing activity progressively
- Return to work at appropriate stage
- Continued wound care
- Attending scheduled follow-ups (day 14, day 28, day 42)

**Typical return-to-work timeline:**
- Minor procedures: 1 to 3 days
- Laser procedures: 3 to 7 days
- Major surgery: 1 to 2 weeks
- Physical work: often 2 to 4 weeks

### Phase 4: Long-Term Recovery (Beyond 6 Weeks)

**Priorities:**
- Full activity resumption
- Long-term prevention practices
- Ongoing monitoring for recurrence
- Addressing underlying risk factors (diabetes, constipation, weight, etc.)

---

## General Principles Across All Recoveries

**Follow instructions exactly.** Discharge instructions are specific to your case. Follow them, do not modify based on how you feel.

**Take medications as prescribed.** Do not stop antibiotics or pain medication early even if you feel better.

**Do not skip follow-up visits.** They exist for a reason. Skipping them means missing early detection of any issue.

**Ask questions.** WhatsApp us, call us, come in. Better to ask a "small" question than to worry silently.

**Report red flags immediately.** Fever, heavy bleeding, severe pain, spreading redness, breathing difficulty. Do not wait.

**Address underlying causes.** Whatever brought you to surgery has an underlying cause. Address it to prevent recurrence.

---

## Diet After Surgery

**General principles:**
- Start with light easily digestible food
- Advance to normal diet over 3 to 5 days
- Include fibre for anorectal cases
- Adequate fluids (2 to 3 litres daily)
- Avoid excessive spicy, oily, or heavy foods during early recovery
- Address any specific dietary needs from your condition

---

## Activity After Surgery

**General principles:**
- Rest immediately after
- Light walking from day 1
- Gradual increase in activity
- No lifting for 2 to 4 weeks depending on procedure
- Return to exercise progressively
- Sexual activity: as guided by procedure

---

## When to Contact Us

**Contact immediately for:**
- Fever above 100.4°F / 38°C
- Heavy or continuous bleeding
- Severe pain not controlled by medication
- Signs of wound infection (spreading redness, foul discharge)
- Inability to pass urine or stool
- Persistent vomiting
- Chest pain, breathing difficulty
- Any severe worsening
- Any concern that worries you

**Standard contact:**
- Appointment/queries: 8208927917
- Emergency (24 hours): 9405404492
- WhatsApp for photos and non-urgent questions

---

## Related Content
- Complete Recovery After Piles Surgery playbook
- Complete Recovery After Fistula Surgery playbook
- Ksharsutra Treatment Guide

# 87. Diet and Lifestyle Guidance

**URL:** `/patients/diet-and-lifestyle/`
**Meta title:** Diet and Lifestyle Guidance | Shri Manmukund Hospital
**Meta description:** Practical diet and lifestyle guidance for patients with anorectal, digestive, and other conditions managed at Shri Manmukund Hospital.

---

## Hero

### Headline
Diet and Lifestyle Guidance

### Sub-headline
Practical, honest guidance on diet, hydration, activity, and lifestyle for patients managing anorectal, digestive, and general health conditions.

---

## Answer-First Summary

Consistent dietary and lifestyle practices are foundational to preventing and managing many conditions treated at our hospital. This guide focuses on practical, sustainable habits: adequate fibre, hydration, regular activity, healthy bowel habits, and specific guidance for common conditions. Small consistent changes matter more than dramatic short-term diets.

---

## Fibre: The Foundation

**Why it matters:**
Adequate fibre softens stool, reduces constipation, prevents straining, and supports gut health. This is central to preventing and managing piles, fissures, and many digestive conditions.

**Target:** 25 to 30 g of fibre per day for adults.

**Good sources:**
- Whole grains (whole wheat, brown rice, oats, ragi, jowar)
- Pulses (lentils, chickpeas, kidney beans, moong dal)
- Vegetables (leafy greens, cabbage, cauliflower, carrots, beans)
- Fruits (apple, papaya, banana, pear, guava, oranges)
- Nuts and seeds (almonds, flaxseeds, chia seeds)

**Practical tips:**
- Include a vegetable serving at both lunch and dinner
- Add whole grains instead of refined grains
- Include a fruit at breakfast and as an evening snack
- Add pulses to your meals regularly

**If you have low fibre currently:**
Increase gradually over 2 weeks to avoid bloating.

---

## Hydration

**Target:** 2 to 3 litres of fluid per day for adults (more in hot weather or with physical activity).

**Best sources:**
- Water (primary source)
- Buttermilk, lassi (moderate amounts)
- Coconut water
- Herbal teas
- Fresh vegetable soups
- Fruits with high water content

**Limit or avoid:**
- Excessive tea, coffee (dehydrating)
- Sugary drinks
- Excessive alcohol

**Practical tips:**
- Start the day with a glass of warm water
- Keep a water bottle at your workspace
- Include water at every meal
- Herbal teas count toward fluid intake

---

## Bowel Habits

**Healthy patterns:**
- Regular bowel movements (frequency varies from thrice daily to thrice weekly is normal)
- Soft, formed stool
- No straining required
- Complete evacuation
- No pain or bleeding

**Common bad habits to correct:**
- Ignoring the urge to defecate
- Prolonged sitting on the toilet (phones, reading)
- Straining
- Poor toilet posture
- Regular use of laxatives without medical guidance

**Good practices:**
- Respond to the urge promptly
- Aim to complete within 5 minutes
- Do not strain
- Use a small footstool to improve posture (feet slightly elevated)
- Use warm water for cleaning where possible

---

## Physical Activity

**Target:** at least 30 minutes of moderate physical activity most days.

**Suitable activities:**
- Walking (accessible for most people)
- Cycling
- Swimming
- Yoga
- Light exercise or gym work

**Benefits for anorectal health:**
- Improves bowel motility
- Reduces constipation
- Maintains healthy weight
- Improves circulation

**Practical tips:**
- Start where you are and build gradually
- Consistency matters more than intensity
- Break into smaller sessions if needed
- Choose activities you enjoy

---

## Specific Condition Guidance

### For Piles and Fissure
- High fibre priority
- Adequate hydration
- Avoid prolonged sitting
- Do not strain
- Warm sitz baths for symptomatic relief

### For Fistula (During Treatment)
- Balanced diet
- Adequate fibre and hydration
- Avoid excessive spicy foods
- Diabetes control if applicable

### For Hyperacidity
- Regular meal times
- Small frequent meals
- Avoid very spicy, oily, fried foods during acute episodes
- Avoid late night eating
- Limit tea, coffee, alcohol
- Manage stress

### For Spine Conditions
- Weight management
- Ergonomic posture
- Regular back-friendly exercise
- Adequate calcium and vitamin D

### For Non-Healing Wounds and Diabetes
- Strict blood sugar control
- Adequate protein intake
- Vitamin and mineral adequacy
- Foot care and inspection (for diabetic patients)

---

## Sustainable Change

The best diet and lifestyle changes are:
- **Small:** you can maintain them
- **Specific:** clear, actionable, not vague
- **Consistent:** daily practice beats occasional heroics
- **Realistic:** fit within your life, not a fantasy version

Perfect adherence for 3 weeks matters less than 80% adherence over 3 years.

# 88. Consolidated FAQ

**URL:** `/patients/faq/`
**Meta title:** Frequently Asked Questions | Shri Manmukund Hospital, Amravati
**Meta description:** Common questions and answers about consultations, treatments, insurance, and services at Shri Manmukund Hospital.

---

## Hero

### Headline
Frequently Asked Questions

### Sub-headline
Answers to questions patients ask most often. Grouped by category for easy navigation.

---

## About the Hospital

**Q: Where is Shri Manmukund Hospital located?**
Plot No 7, Bapatwadi, Vivekanand Colony to Radient Hospital Road, Amravati 444604, Maharashtra.

**Q: What are the OPD timings?**
Dr. Vipin: Monday to Saturday, 1.00 PM to 4.30 PM and 6.00 PM to 8.30 PM.
Dr. Swati: Monday to Saturday, 2.30 PM to 4.30 PM and 6.00 PM to 8.00 PM.
Sunday: prior appointment only.
Emergency: 24 hours.

**Q: Is the hospital open on holidays?**
Emergency services are available 24 hours including holidays. Regular OPD is by prior appointment on holidays.

**Q: How do I reach the hospital?**
By car: our address is easily found on Google Maps. Free parking is available near the hospital.
By auto: any auto in Amravati can bring you; mention Bapatwadi, Vivekanand Colony.
From outside Amravati: by road via NH53 or by rail to Amravati Railway Station, then local transport.

---

## Booking and Consultation

**Q: How do I book an appointment?**
Call 8208927917 during hours, or send a WhatsApp message. You can also walk in during OPD hours, though a booked appointment reduces waiting time.

**Q: Can I consult online first before coming?**
Yes, for preliminary discussions. Call or WhatsApp 8208927917 to arrange.

**Q: How long is a consultation?**
First consultation typically 30 to 45 minutes. Follow-up visits are shorter.

**Q: What is the consultation fee?**
Please call for current fees.

**Q: Can I request a specific doctor?**
Yes. Please mention Dr. Vipin or Dr. Swati when booking.

---

## Treatment and Procedures

**Q: What conditions do you treat?**
See our Services section. Broadly: anorectal conditions, general surgery, Ayurveda and Panchakarma, spine care, female specialty care, Ksharsutra, laser proctology, non-surgical piles treatment, and more.

**Q: Do I always need surgery?**
No. Many conditions are managed without surgery. We recommend surgery only when it is genuinely the best option for your case.

**Q: What types of anaesthesia are used?**
Local anaesthesia for many minor procedures. Spinal or short general anaesthesia for major procedures. Discussed and chosen based on the specific procedure.

**Q: Are your procedures day-care?**
Many procedures are day-care (same-day discharge): rubber band ligation, sclerotherapy, laser haemorrhoidoplasty, laser fistula treatment, and others. Major procedures may require 1 to 3 days of admission.

**Q: How long is recovery?**
Depends on the procedure. Detailed recovery timelines are in our Knowledge Hub playbooks.

---

## Insurance and Payment

**Q: Do you accept insurance?**
Shri Manmukund Hospital is registered under ROHINI (Registry of Hospitals in Network of Insurance). Currently, we carry select cases through partner hospital arrangements for cashless treatment while our own cashless empanelment is under process. Please call 8208927917 for current information on your specific insurer.

**Q: What payment methods are accepted?**
Cash, UPI, net banking, and bank transfer. Insurance details as per your specific policy.

**Q: Do you provide detailed billing?**
Yes. Detailed billing for insurance and personal records is provided.

---

## Female Patients

**Q: Can I request Dr. Swati specifically?**
Yes. Please mention this when booking on 8208927917.

**Q: Can I bring a female companion?**
Yes. Companions (mother, sister, husband, friend) are welcome during consultation and examination per your preference.

**Q: Is examination done in privacy?**
Yes. All examinations happen in a private examination area with dignity maintained.

**Q: What if I am uncomfortable discussing my symptoms?**
Take your time. We do not rush consultations. You can also send an initial WhatsApp message describing your concern before the visit.

---

## For Patients Travelling from a Distance

**Q: I am travelling from outside Amravati. What should I know?**
Please call ahead so we can plan your visit and any procedure efficiently. Bring all previous medical records. If a procedure is planned, we may be able to schedule investigations and procedure closer together to minimise travel.

**Q: Is there accommodation nearby?**
Yes. Amravati has several accommodation options at different budgets. We can provide guidance.

**Q: Can follow-up be done remotely?**
For non-critical follow-ups, WhatsApp consultation with photos is possible. Critical follow-ups usually require an in-person visit. For Ksharsutra treatment specifically, weekly in-person visits are needed but we can offer IFTAK (a modified technique) for patients where weekly visits over months are impractical.

---

## Emergencies

**Q: What if I have an emergency?**
Call 9405404492 (24 hours). Our emergency line is monitored day and night.

**Q: What counts as an emergency related to your services?**
Heavy rectal bleeding, severe unrelenting abdominal or perianal pain, high fever with wound issues, paraphimosis with swelling, acute abscess with fever, any post-operative emergency, and any situation you find urgent.

**Q: If it is a life-threatening emergency, should I come to you?**
For life-threatening emergencies (heart attack, stroke, major trauma), call the local emergency services (108) or go to the nearest emergency-capable hospital. Our emergency care is specific to our specialty scope.

---

## For More Questions
Call: 8208927917
Emergency: 9405404492
WhatsApp: available on both numbers

---

Cash, UPI, net banking, and bank transfer. Insurance details as per your specific policy.

**Q: Do you provide detailed billing?**
Yes. Detailed billing for insurance and personal records is provided.

---

## Female Patients

**Q: Can I request Dr. Swati specifically?**
Yes. Please mention this when booking on 8208927917.

**Q: Can I bring a female companion?**
Yes. Companions (mother, sister, husband, friend) are welcome during consultation and examination per your preference.

**Q: Is examination done in privacy?**
Yes. All examinations happen in a private examination area with dignity maintained.

**Q: What if I am uncomfortable discussing my symptoms?**
Take your time. We do not rush consultations. You can also send an initial WhatsApp message describing your concern before the visit.

---

## For Patients Travelling from a Distance

**Q: I am travelling from outside Amravati. What should I know?**
Please call ahead so we can plan your visit and any procedure efficiently. Bring all previous medical records. If a procedure is planned, we may be able to schedule investigations and procedure closer together to minimise travel.

**Q: Is there accommodation nearby?**
Yes. Amravati has several accommodation options at different budgets. We can provide guidance.

**Q: Can follow-up be done remotely?**
For non-critical follow-ups, WhatsApp consultation with photos is possible. Critical follow-ups usually require an in-person visit. For Ksharsutra treatment specifically, weekly in-person visits are needed but we can offer IFTAK (a modified technique) for patients where weekly visits over months are impractical.

---

## Emergencies

**Q: What if I have an emergency?**
Call 9405404492 (24 hours). Our emergency line is monitored day and night.

**Q: What counts as an emergency related to your services?**
Heavy rectal bleeding, severe unrelenting abdominal or perianal pain, high fever with wound issues, paraphimosis with swelling, acute abscess with fever, any post-operative emergency, and any situation you find urgent.

**Q: If it is a life-threatening emergency, should I come to you?**
For life-threatening emergencies (heart attack, stroke, major trauma), call the local emergency services (108) or go to the nearest emergency-capable hospital. Our emergency care is specific to our specialty scope.

---

Emergency: 9405404492
WhatsApp: available on both numbers

## Introduction

Shri Manmukund Hospital ("we", "our", "us") is committed to protecting the privacy of visitors to our website (www.shrimanmukundhospital.com) and patients who consult us. This Privacy Policy explains what information we collect, how we use it, how we protect it, and your rights regarding your information.

By using our website, you consent to the practices described in this policy.

---

## Information We Collect

### Information You Provide
- Contact information (name, phone number, email) when you use our enquiry form, book an appointment, or send us a message
- Medical information you share during consultation (this is protected as confidential medical information)
- Any other information you voluntarily provide

### Information Collected Automatically
- IP address
- Browser type and version
- Device information
- Pages visited on our site
- Time and date of visit
- Referring website

We use analytics tools (such as Google Analytics) to understand website usage. These tools collect anonymised or aggregated data.

### Cookies
Our website uses cookies to improve your browsing experience. See our Cookie Policy for details.

---

## How We Use Your Information

- To respond to your enquiries and appointment requests
- To provide medical consultation and care
- To send appointment reminders and follow-up communications
- To improve our website and services
- To comply with legal and regulatory obligations
- For internal administrative purposes

We do not sell your information to third parties.

---

## Medical Information

Medical information shared during consultation is protected by medical confidentiality standards under Indian medical practice regulations. This information is:
- Shared only with treating doctors and authorised medical staff
- Not disclosed to third parties without your consent, except as required by law
- Retained as per applicable medical record retention requirements
- Used to provide you with medical care

---

## Sharing of Information

We may share your information with:
- Treating doctors and medical staff at our hospital
- Referred specialists (with your consent) if your case requires referral
- Insurance providers (with your consent) for claim processing
- Legal or regulatory authorities where required by law
- Service providers who help us operate our website (bound by confidentiality)

We do not share your medical information for marketing purposes.

---

## Data Security

We take reasonable measures to protect your information from unauthorised access, alteration, disclosure, or destruction. However, no method of internet transmission or electronic storage is 100% secure. We cannot guarantee absolute security.

---

## Your Rights

You have the right to:
- Access the personal information we hold about you
- Request correction of inaccurate information
- Request deletion of your information (subject to legal and medical record retention requirements)
- Withdraw consent for specific uses of your information
- Opt out of non-essential communications

To exercise these rights, contact us at info@shrimanmukundhospital.com or 8208927917.

---

## Retention of Information

- Website enquiry information: retained for reasonable duration to respond and follow up
- Medical records: retained as per applicable medical record retention requirements
- Marketing communications preferences: retained until you opt out

---

## Third-Party Links

Our website may contain links to third-party websites. This Privacy Policy applies only to our website. We are not responsible for the privacy practices of third-party websites.

---

## Children's Privacy

Our website is not directed at children under 13. We do not knowingly collect information from children under 13. If you believe we have collected information from a child under 13, please contact us to have it removed.

## Changes to This Policy
